articles.heading: Purpose of this Law
Interpretation In this Law
articles.text:
(a) “accessible format copy” means a copy of
a work in a manner or form which gives a
person who is visually impaired or print
disabled access to the work, including
permitting the person to have access as
feasibly and comfortably as a person
without visual impairment or other print
disability;
(b) “anonymous work” means a work which
does not indicate the name or pseudonym
of the author;
62
(c) “ARIPO” means the African Regional
Intellectual Property Organisation;
(d) “audio-visual work” means a work that
consists of a series of related images which
impart the impression of motion, with or
without accompanying sounds, susceptible
of being made visible and where
accompanied by sounds, susceptible of
being made audible;
(e) “Author” means a person who created a
work;
(f) “authorised entity” means an entity that
is authorised or recognised by the
government to provide education,
instructional training, adaptive reading or
information access to persons who are
visually impaired or print disabled on a
non-profit basis;
(g) “basic application” means an application
for registration of a mark filed with the
competent authority and which is used as a
basis for the filing of an international
application;
63
(h) “basic registration” means a mark
registered by the competent authority and
which is used as the basis for the filing of
an international application;
(i) “broadcasting” means the transmission
by wireless means for public reception of
sounds or of images and sounds or of the
representations thereof, including
transmission by satellite, and transmission
of encrypted signals where the means for
decrypting are provided to the public by the
broadcasting organisation or with its
consent;
(j) “certification mark” means a sign or
combination of signs capable of
designating any common characteristic,
including quality, origin or methods of
production of goods and services and
which are used under the control of the
owner of the sign;
(k) “unfair competition” means any act or
practice that is, in the course of industrial
or commercial activities, contrary to honest
practices when the purpose or the
consequence is to obtain trade advantage
64
parallel to those of the producer of services
or to some products similar to those of
another person;
(l) “collective mark” means a visible sign
enabling the origin, quality, or any other
common feature of product or service of
users of the mark to be distinguished from
those of others;
(m)“collective work” means a work created
by several persons represented by a person
and created in such a way that the
contributions and identities of individual
contributors to the work cannot be
separately identified;
(n) “communication to the public” means
the transmission to the public by any means
of a work, a performance or a phonogram,
or an audio-visual fixation, or a broadcast
in such a way that it can be perceived by
persons outside the normal circle of a
family and its closest social acquaintances
at a place or places so distant from the
place where the transmission originates
that, without the transmission, the work,
performance, phonogram or audio-visual
fixation or broadcast would not be
perceivable, including the making
65
available of the work or other protected
subject matter in such a way that members
of the public may access it from a place and
at a time individually chosen by them;
(o) competent authority” means the organ in
charge of protection of intellectual
property;
(p) “complete specification” means a
document, which discloses all details of an
invention in a sufficiently clear and
complete manner, so as to enable a person
having ordinary skills in the art to apply the
invention;
(q) “compulsory licence” means an
authorisation to use a patented invention,
utility model, industrial design or a layoutdesign of integrated circuit, granted to a
third party by the Minister without the
agreement of the owner of rights;
(r) “computer program” means instructions
expressed in words, codes, schemes or in
any other form, which is capable, when
incorporated into a medium that the
66
computer can read, of causing a computer
or any electronic device having
information-processing capabilities to
perform or achieve a particular task or
result;
(s) “copy of the work” means the result of
any act of reproduction of a work;
(t) “copyright” means a right granted to an
author allowing him or her to control and
prevent unauthorised use of his or her
work;
(u) “copy of a phonogram” means any
medium containing sounds taken directly
or indirectly from a phonogram and
incorporating all or a substantial part of the
sounds fixed on that phonogram;
(v) “derivative work” means a work created
on the basis of one or several pre-existing
works;
(w)“exclusive licence” means a licence
contract that confers on the licensee the
right to exploit the intellectual property to
67
the exclusion of all other persons,
including the right owner;
(x) “expression of folklore” means a form or
manner in which cultural knowledge is
expressed or manifested, including:
a) folktales, folk poetry and folk
riddles;
b) folk songs and instrumental folk
music;
c) folk dances and folk plays;
d) productions of folk arts in
particular, drawings, paintings,
carvings, sculptures, pottery,
terra-cotta, mosaic, woodwork,
metal ware, jewellery and
indigenous textiles;
(y) “fixation” means the embodiment of
sounds, images or both or of the
68
representations thereof, from which they
can be perceived, reproduced or
communicated through a device;
(z) “geographical indication” means a sign
identifying a product as originating in the
territory, region or locality of a country,
where a quality, reputation or other specific
feature of that product may be attributed
essentially to its geographical origin;
(aa) “industry” means a human activity
leading to the production of goods or
services for economic purposes;
(bb) “industrial designs” means an
assembly of lines, colours or shape of an
industrial or craft product which serves as
a model for the manufacture of an
industrial or craft product;
(cc) “industrial property title” means a
certificate of registration issued by the
competent authority in respect of:
69
(i) an invention;
(ii) a utility model;
(iii)an industrial design;
(iv)a mark, collective mark or
certification mark;
(v) geographical indication;
(vi)a layout-design and integrated
circuit.
(dd) integrated circuit” means a product,
in its final or an intermediate form, in
which the interconnections form an
integral part of the body or surface of a
component which is intended to carry out
an electronic function;
(ee) “international application” means an
application to obtain a patent, registration
of a mark and of industrial design filed
under the relevant international treaty;
70
(ff) “international bureau” means the Bureau
of the World Intellectual Property
Organisation;
(gg) “international register” means the
official collection of data concerning
international registrations of industrial
property maintained by the International
Bureau;
(hh) “invention” means an idea of an
inventor which permits in practice to find
solution to a given technical or
technological problem, that may consist of,
or relate to, a product or a process;
(ii) “making available to the public” means
to make available to the public a work or
other protected subject matter by wire or
wireless means in such a way that the
public or natural person may access it from
a place and at a time individually chosen by
them;
(jj) “layout-design of integrated circuits”
means a three-dimensional arrangement in
whatever form of the elements, at least one
71
of which is active, and of all or part of the
interconnections of an integrated circuit, or
such a three-dimensional arrangement,
prepared for an integrated circuit intended
to be manufactured;
(kk) “contractual licence” means a
contract or agreement by which a person
grants permission to another person to use
his or her intellectual property right;
(ll) “mark” means a visible sign enabling a
product or service of a person to be
distinguished from that of another person;
(mm) “Minister” means the Minister in
charge of Intellectual Property;
(nn) “non-exclusive licence” means the
licence contract that confers on two or
many persons the right to exploit the
industrial property right;
72
(oo) “orphan work” means a work which
is protected by copyright but for which the
owner of rights is difficult or impossible to
locate;
(pp) “patent” means a title issued by a
competent authority to protect an
invention;
(qq) “performing artist” means an actor,
singer, musician, dancer or other person
who acts, sings, delivers or otherwise
performs a work;
(rr) “person having ordinary skills in the
art” means a citizen of Rwanda, or any
person with habitual residence located in
Rwanda, who carries out his or her
profession in Rwanda, having acquired
knowledge, expertise and experience in the
technical field of the claimed invention;
(ss)“person who is blind, visually impaired,
or otherwise print disabled” means a
person who:
(i) is blind;
73
(ii) has a visual impairment or a
perceptual or reading disability
which cannot be improved to give
visual function substantially
equivalent to that of a person who
has no such impairment or
disability and so is unable to read
printed works to substantially the
same degree as a person without
an impairment or disability;
(iii) otherwise unable, through
physical disability, to hold or
manipulate a book or to focus or
move the eyes to the extent that
would be normally acceptable for
reading.
(tt) “phonogram” means the fixation of the
sounds of a performance or of other sounds
or of a representation of sounds other than
in the form of a fixation incorporated in
audio-visual work;
(uu) “phonogram producer” means a
person that makes the first fixation of the
sounds of a performance;
74
(vv) “photographic work” means a
photograph taken through recording of
light or other radiation in any medium on
which an image is produced or from which
an image may be produced through
chemical, electronic or other means;
(ww) “provisional specification” means a
document, which broadly, but not
completely, discloses an inventive concept,
filed mainly to secure a priority date when
the inventor needs more time to work out
the details of his invention;
(xx) “public performance” means reciting,
playing, dancing, acting or otherwise
performing the work, either directly or by
means of any device or process. In the case
of an audio-visual work, it means the
showing of its images in sequence or
making its accompanying sounds audible.
In the case of a phonogram, it means
making the recorded sounds audible, in
each case at a place or at places where
persons outside the normal circle of the
family and its closest acquaintances are or
75
can be present, irrespective of whether they
are or can be present at the same place and
time, or at different places or times, and
where the performance can be perceived
without the need for communication to the
public;
(yy) “published work” means a copy of a
work or a phonogram which was
disseminated to the public with the
permission of the author or right holder by
way of selling, renting, lending,
transferring or making available for
electronic retrieval;
(zz) “related right” means the copyright of
an artist performer, producer of
phonograms or of broadcasting
organisation without wires;
(aaa) “rental” means transfer of possession
of the original or a copy of a work or
phonogram for a limited period of time for
profit-making purposes;
(bbb) “reproduction” means making of one
or more copies of a work or performance
76
or phonogram or a part of both, in any
manner or form, including recording of
sounds and images, and permanent or
temporary storage of the work or
performance or phonogram in electronic
form;
(ccc) “rights management information”
means any information which identifies the
author, the work, performing artists,
phonogram producer, the phonogram, the
broadcaster, the broadcast, the owner of
any right, or any information about the
terms and conditions of use of the work and
other works, any numbers or codes that
represent such information, when any of
these items of information is attached to a
copy of a work, a fixed performance, on a
copy of a phonogram or a fixed broadcast,
or appears in connection with the
broadcasting, communication or making
available to the public of a work, a fixed
performance, a phonogram or a broadcast;
77
(ddd) “semi exclusive licence” means a
licence contract that confers on the holder
the right to exploit the licenced industrial
property right to the exclusion of all other
persons, except the right owner;
(eee) “trade name” means a name or
designation identifying and distinguishing
the business of a person from that of
another person;
(fff) “utility model” means a technical
creation that consists of a new shape or
configuration of an object, or of a
component of an object, that increases its
functionality or utility;
(ggg) “work” means any literary, artistic or
scientific work;
(hhh) “work derived from folklore” means
a work predominantly created on the basis
of elements borrowed from the folklore;
(iii)“work of applied art” means an artistic
creation that has utilitarian function or is
incorporated in a useful article, whether a
78
work of handicraft or one produced on an
industrial scale;
(jjj)“work of joint authorship” means a work
produced by collaboration of two or more
authors;
(kkk) “person” means a natural person or
legal entity whether public or private.

articles.heading: Scope of this Law This Law applies to
articles.text:
(a) industrial property;
(b) copyrights and related rights.
TITLE II: INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY
CHAPTER ONE: CATEGORIES OF
INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY
79

articles.heading: Categories of industrial property Industrial property applies to the exclusive right to use the following
Patentable invention An invention is patentable if
Novelty of an invention (1) An invention is new if it is not anticipated by the prior art
articles.text:
(2) The assessment of the prior art takes into
consideration the disclosure of the
invention that has been disclosed anywhere
in the world by publication in intangible
form, by oral disclosure, by use or in any
other way, prior to the filing date or where
applicable, the priority date of the patent
application claiming the invention.
(3) However, the disclosure of the invention is
not considered when determining the
novelty of an invention if:
(a) it occurs within 12 months preceding
the filing date of a patent application;
81
(b) It occurs before the priority date of
patent application, where applicable;
(c) it has resulted directly or indirectly
from acts performed by the applicant;
(d) it has resulted from an abuse
committed by a third party with regard
to the applicant or the rightful
predecessor.
(4) In accordance with Paragraph (3) of this
Article, the disclosure of the invention is
not considered when determining the
novelty of an invention if it occurs within
12 months preceding the filing date of a
patent application or where applicable, the
priority date of the application claiming the
invention in respect of goods officially
exhibited or officially recognised in
international exhibitions held on the
territory of the Republic of Rwanda. The
applicant transmits to the competent
authority at the time of the application, the
proof of the item exhibited and the date of
the recognised international exhibition.
82

articles.heading: Inventive step An invention is considered as involving an inventive step if, having regard to the prior art
articles.text:
relevant to the patent application claiming the
invention, it would not have been obvious to a
person having ordinary skill in the art.

articles.heading: Industrial applicability of an invention An invention is industrially applicable if its subject matter can be made or used in an
articles.text: industry.

articles.heading: Filing the application for a patent (1) A patent application is filed with the competent authority
articles.text:
(2) The patent application contains the
following:
(a) a request for the grant of a patent;
(b) a description of the invention;
83
(c) one or more claims of novelty in the
invention;
(d) one or more drawings illustrating the
invention where necessary;
(e) an abstract of invention;
(f) the proof of payment of a prescribed
fee.
(3) An Order of the Minister may
determine other items to be submitted
to the competent authority at the time
of filing a patent application.
(4) The competent authority sets the date
of receipt of the application for a
patent as the filing date, and classifies
the invention according to the
International Classification.

articles.heading: Request for the grant of a patent (1) A request for the grant of a patent is made by filling in a relevant form
articles.text:
prescribed by the competent authority.
84
(2) The application submission is subject
to payment of a prescribed fee.
(3) However, the modalities for filing of an
application for patent with regard to
national security and law and order are
determined by an Order of the Minister
in charge of Rwanda Defence Forces.

articles.heading: Description of an invention (1) The description of an invention explains and discloses the invention in
articles.text:
a manner sufficiently clear, complete
and intelligible so as to be used by a
person skilled in the art.
(2) The description indicates the best way
to use the invention known to the
applicant at the filing date or, where
priority is claimed, at the priority date
of the application. Drawings may be
provided to understand the invention, if
considered necessary.
(3) The competent authority may, at any
time before the grant of the patent,
require the description in foreign patent
applications to be adapted to the
85
ordinary skills in the art of a citizen of
Rwanda, or any foreign citizen with
habitual residence in the Republic of
Rwanda and who carries out his or her
profession in the Republic of Rwanda,
so as to ensure technology transfer and
dissemination.

articles.heading: Assessing the sufficiency of disclosure (1) During assessment of sufficiency of disclosure, the disclosure contained in
articles.text:
the description, claims and drawings,
as established on the date on which the
sufficiency of disclosure was
examined, are taken into account.
(2) The disclosure of claims of an
invention is considered to be clear and
concise when it is sufficient and fully
supported by the description in a way
that the person skilled in the art can, on
the date of the application, use the
invention without necessarily making
recourse to trials.
86

articles.heading: Examining the sufficient disclosure of a micro-organism The content of a disclosure of claim for an
articles.text:
invention of a micro-organism or an invention
which requires, for its performance, the use of
a micro-organism which is not available to the
public at the date of filing is treated as clear
and complete enough for the invention to be
performed by a person skilled in the art if the
following conditions are met:
(a) a culture of the micro-organism has
been effected with an international
depositary authority which is
recognised under the Budapest Treaty;
(b) the application as filed gives such
relevant and sufficient information on
the characteristics of the microorganism;
(c) the date when the culture was
deposited, the name of an international
depositary authority, and the accession
number of the deposit are given in the
description of the application; and
87
(d) the receipt of the deposit issued by an
international depositary authority is
filed with the patent application not
later than 12 months from the filing
date of the patent application.

articles.heading: Claim of an invention (1) The scope of the protection granted for an invention or an innovation is determined
articles.text:
by the extent of the claim or claims of that
invention.
(2) The claim of an invention must be clear
and concise. Such a claim is solely based
on the description of the invention.
(3) The claim of an invention as well as the
description and drawings may be used to
interpret the claims of the invention.
88

articles.heading: Abstract of the invention (1) The abstract summarises the invention, description and claims of the invention
articles.text:
and must be used exclusively for
technical information purposes.
(2) However, the competent authority does
not consider the abstract of the invention
while assessing the scope of protection.

articles.heading: Unity of an invention (1) An application for registration relates to one invention or to a group of inventions
articles.text:
linked to form a single general inventive or
innovative concept.
(2) However, unity of an invention is not a
ground for opposition to or invalidation of
a patent that the patent comprises more
than one invention or the group of
inventions which are not linked to form a
single inventive concept.
89

articles.heading: Divisional application (1) Until the competent authority confirms that the application meets the requirements for
articles.text:
the grant of the patent, the applicant may
divide the application into more than one
divisional application.
(2) However, each divisional application does
not disclose matter extending beyond that
disclosed in the original application as
filed.
(3) Each divisional application has the filing
date and, where appropriate, the priority is
the date of the initial application.

articles.heading: Application accompanied by a provisional specification (1) The application for a patent may be
articles.text:
accompanied by a provisional
specification.
(2) Where an application for a patent is
accompanied by a provisional
specification, a final specification is filed
90
within 12 months from the date of filing the
first application.
(3) If the final specification is filed within the
period of 12 months provided for in
Paragraph (2) of this Article, the priority
date becomes the date on which the
application accompanied by a provisional
specification was filed.
(4) If the final specification is not filed within
the period provided in Paragraph (2) of this
Article, the application is considered to be
abandoned and is removed from the
register.

articles.heading: Multiple applications accompanied with a provisional specification (1) An applicant may file multiple applications
articles.text:
accompanied by provisional specifications.
(2) If the application referred to in Paragraph
(1) of this Article is filed in respect of
inventions which are cognate or of which
91
one is a modification of another and the
competent authority is of the opinion that
the whole of such inventions are such as to
constitute a single invention and may be
granted one patent, the competent authority
may allow one final specification to be
filed within 12 months from the date of
filing of the earliest provisional
specification.

articles.heading: Conversion of application for a patent into a provisional application (1) The applicant for a patent may, at any time
articles.text:
prior to the decision on the application,
request the competent authority to convert
his or her application into a provisional
application.
(2) Where an application for a patent is
accompanied by specification considered
as final, the competent authority may, upon
request by the applicant and within the
period of 12 months from the date of initial
application, allow the final specification to
be considered as a provisional
specification and the application is not
discontinued.
92

articles.heading: Request to post-date the filing date over the provisional application If a complete specification has been filed in
articles.text:
pursuance of an application for a patent
accompanied by a provisional specification,
the competent authority may, at the request of
the applicant before the grant of patent, cancel
the provisional specification and post-date the
application to the date of filing of the final
specification.

articles.heading: Content of a provisional application (1) The provisional application contains the following –
articles.text:
(a) a relevant provisional application form
prescribed by the competent authority
and which is filled in by the applicant;
93
(b) description of invention without
specification or disclosure;
(c) one or several drawings describing the
invention, where applicable;
(d) the title of invention; and
(e) the proof of payment of application
fee.
(2) Where necessary, the competent authority
requires that the drawings be supplied for
the purpose of provisional application and
a supplied drawing is, unless the
Competent authority otherwise directs,
considered to form part of the
specification, and the reference under this
Law.
(3) If the competent authority considers that an
application should be further supplemented
by a model or sample of anything
illustrating the invention or alleged to
constitute an invention, such sample or
model as the competent authority requires
to be furnished before the final application
is examined.
94

articles.heading: Matters excluded from patent protection (1) The following matters are excluded from patent protection even if they
articles.text:
otherwise constitute patentable
invention:
(a) discoveries, scientific theories and
mathematical methods;
(b) schemes, rules or methods for doing
business, performing purely mental
acts or playing games;
(c) methods for treatment of the human or
animal body by surgery or therapy, as
well as diagnostic methods practiced
on the human or animal body; but not
including products for use in any of
those methods;
(d) substances, even if purified,
synthesised or otherwise isolated from
nature, but not including the processes
of isolating those substances from their
original environment;
95
(e) known substances for which a new use
has been discovered, but not including
the new use itself where it constitutes
an invention and where that use results
in the enhancement of the known
efficacy of that substance;
(f) plants and animal varieties, including
their parts, other than micro-organisms
and essentially biological processes for
the production of plants or animals and
their parts, other than non-biological
and microbiological processes and
products obtained from those
processes;
(g) inventions whose commercial use is
contrary to public order and morality;
(h) pharmaceutical products;
(i) mere presentations of data;
(j) computer programs per se, software
and their related databases.
96
(2) An Order of the Minister in charge of
health determines pharmaceutical
products referred to in Subparagraph
(h) of this Article which are excluded
from patent protection.
(3) The provisions of Subparagraph (j) of
this Article are not applicable to the
following inventions:
(a) process inventions which, in whole or
in part, consist of steps that are
performed by a computer and are
directed by a computer program;
(b) product inventions consisting of
elements of a computer-implemented
invention, including in particular:
(i) a machine-readable computer
program code stored on a tangible
medium such as a disk or computer
memory;
(ii) a general-purpose computer whose
novelty over the prior art arises
primarily due to its combination
with a specific computer program;
97
(iii)a computer program with any
additional features such as
technical features or in its technical
application to industry and in
combination with hardware.
(4) An applicant for a patent who has filed
patent applications for computer
programs and computer-related
inventions listed in paragraph (3) of
this article waives his or her right of
seeking copyright protection for the
same subject matter.
Section 2: Examination and grant of the
patent

articles.heading: Examination of patent application (1) Before examining the substance of the application for a patent, the competent
articles.text:
authority determines whether the
following are complied with:
98
(a) the invention to which the application
relates is not excluded from
patentability;
(b) the application meets the requirements
relating to the form and content of the
application.
(2) If the requirements have not been met,
the competent authority invites the
applicant to comply with relevant
requirements within 14 days from the
date of notification.
(3) If the applicant meets the relevant
requirements referred to in Paragraph (2)
of this Article, the date of receipt of the
corrected application is considered as the
application filing date.
(4) If the requirements to be met relate to
drawings, the competent authority
considers the date of receipt of the initial
application as the application filing date.
(5) If the applicant does not comply with the
relevant requirements or complies with
them after the prescribed period, the
application is considered as withdrawn.
99

articles.heading: Amendment of the patent application during examination (1) If the competent authority has not
articles.text:
confirmed whether or not the application
meets the requirements for the grant of the
patent, the applicant may amend the
application.
(2) However, an amendment of an application
for a patent is not allowed if it discloses
matters extending beyond those disclosed
in the initial application.

articles.heading: Examination of the substance of the patent application During the examination of the substance of the
articles.text:
patent application, the competent authority
considers the following:
(a) results of any search or examination
report which was carried out by a
specialised agency of the Republic of
Rwanda or an external organisation
conducting search or examination
100
(b) results of any search, examination
report or decision provided in
accordance with Article 252 of this
Law;
(c) results of any international search
report and any international
preliminary examination report
established in accordance with relevant
international convention to which
Rwanda is a party in relation to the
application filed in the Republic of
Rwanda.

articles.heading: Publication of the patent application (1) The competent authority publishes the patent application in the Official
Effects of publication of the patent application (1) From the date of publication of application until the patent is granted,
articles.text:
the applicant has the same privileges
and rights as he or she would have if
the patent were granted.
(2) However, if an application for a patent
is successfully opposed, the privileges
and rights become null as from the date
of the opposition.
102

articles.heading: Opposition to the granting of the patent (1) An interested person may oppose the granting of the patent after obtaining the
articles.text:
full contents of the patent application.
(2) An Order of the Minister determines
modalities to make opposition to the
granting of the patent.

articles.heading: Appeal against a decision on the opposition to the granting of the patent (1) An interested person may appeal, against a
articles.text:
decision on the opposition to the granting
of the patent, before the Commission of
Appeal, within three months from the date
of notification of the decision of the
competent authority.
(2) An Order of the Minister determines the
composition and functioning of the
Commission of Appeal.
103

articles.heading: Grant or refusal of the patent (1) If the application meets the requirements for patentability, the competent authority
articles.text:
does the following:
(a) issues to the applicant a certificate of
the grant of the patent;
(b) records the patent in the register of
patents;
(2) Competent authority makes available a
copy of the patent to any person who
requests for it upon payment of prescribed
fees.
(3) The competent authority rejects the
application if it does not meet the
requirements for patentability and notifies,
in writing, the applicant within seven days
from the date on which the decision was
made.
A
104

articles.heading: Patent publication Within the period of three months from the date of the grant of the patent, the competent
articles.text:
authority publishes, the patent and its abstract
in the Rwanda.

articles.heading: Amendment of the patent file (1) The competent authority, upon request of the patent owner, may make amendments
articles.text:
to patent file or drawings intended to limit
the scope of the conferred patent
protection.
(2) However, the competent authority cannot
make amendment to the patent file if:
a) on the basis of which the patent has
been granted, the amendment
introduces new matters or matters in
substance not disclosed in the patent
file before amendment;
105
b) the patent file as amended would
include a claim not based on matters
disclosed in the patent file before
amendment.

articles.heading: Invalidation of a patent (1) An interested person may apply to the competent court to invalidate a patent if at
articles.text:
least one of the following grounds is
established:
(a) the invention is not new;
(b) the invention does not involve an
inventive step;
(c) the invention is not industrially
applicable;
(d) the invention relates to a matter
excluded from patentability;
(e) the applicant is not the inventor or does
not have the right to apply for the
patent;
106
(f) the invention is not sufficiently clearly,
completely and intelligibly described
by the patent-holder.
(2) The competent court may, instead of
invalidating the patent certificate, transfer
such certificate to the person who requested
for its invalidation where that person
proves to be the inventor and has requested
the registration be made on his or her name.
(3) The interested person or the person that the
court declared to be the inventor notifies
the competent authority of the final
decision of the court to invalidate the patent
so as to:
(a) record the court decision in the register
of patents;
(b) mark the patent as invalidated in the
register of patents;
(c) publish a notice referring to the
decision of the court within a period of
30 days from the date of notification of
the court decision.
107

articles.heading: Effects of invalidation of a patent (1) If the grounds for invalidation of a patent are established with respect to a
articles.text:
part of the invention, only the
corresponding claim is invalidated.
(2) The patent, claim or part of a claim that
has been invalidated is deemed null and
void as from the date of the grant of the
patent.
Section 3: Rights conferred by the patent

articles.heading: Rights conferred by the patent (1) The patent confers on the owner the exclusive rights to use the patented
articles.text:
invention in the Republic of Rwanda.
(2) The patent also confers on the owner
the exclusive rights to stop the use of
the patented invention, by any person
without authorisation by the owner.
108
(3) Use of a patented invention means at
least one of the following acts:
(a) where the patent has been granted in
respect of a product:
(i) making, importing, offering for
sale, selling and using the
product;
(ii) stocking the product for the
purposes of offering it for sale,
selling or using it;
(b) where the patent has been granted in
respect of:
(i) using the process;
(ii) carrying out the acts referred to in
Subparagraph (a) of Paragraph (3) of
this Article as regards to a product
resulting directly from the use of the
process.

articles.heading: Civil proceedings against infringement of patent rights (1) The patent owner initiates civil
articles.text:
proceedings in the competent court
109
against a person who uses the patented
invention or facilitates the use of the
patented invention without his or her
authorisation.
(2) If there is a co-ownership over a patent,
each owner may initiate separate
proceedings, without consent from
each of the owners, for infringement of
the patent rights against any person
who uses the patented invention
without the authorisation of all the
owners.

articles.heading: Joint ownership of the patent (1) If two or more persons have made an invention together, the right to apply
articles.text:
for registration or a certificate belongs
to each of them.
(2) In the absence of an agreement
between the parties, co-owners of a
patent may separately transfer their
shares in the application and prevent
any person from using their
application, but may only jointly
licence any third person to do any of
the acts referred to in this Law.
110

articles.heading: Naming the inventor (1) An inventor is named as such in the application unless he or she provides
articles.text:
the competent authority with a written
declaration indicating that he or she
does not wish to be named as an
inventor.
(2) promise or undertaking to make such a
declaration, made with regard to any
person by the inventor has no effect.

articles.heading: Limitations to patent rights (1) The rights conferred by the patent do not extend to
articles.text:
(a) use of the patented invention on foreign
machines, ships, land vehicles and
spacecrafts that temporarily or
accidentally enter the airspace, waters
or land of the Republic of Rwanda;
111
(b) acts relating to a patented invention
carried out for scientific and
technological research purposes and
for public non-profit use;
(c) acts performed in the Republic of
Rwanda by a person who, in good faith
and on the filing date where priority is
claimed, on the date of the application
for priority on the basis of which the
right of priority was granted, was using
the invention or was making effective
and serious preparations to use it,
insofar as these acts do not differ, in
their nature or purpose, from previous
effective or envisaged use;
(d) acts done privately and on a noncommercial scale, or for noncommercial purposes, if they do not
significantly prejudice the economic
interests of the patent owner;
(e) extemporaneous preparation for
individual cases in a pharmacy of a
112
medicine, in accordance with a medical
prescription or acts concerning the
medicine to be prepared;
(f) products, which have been put on the
market in the Republic of Rwanda or
abroad by the owner of the patent or a
person authorised by him or her.
(2) The right of the prior patent user referred
to in Subparagraph (c) of Paragraph (1) of
this Article to may be transferred or
devolved the enterprise or to the company,
or to part of enterprise or part of company
in which the use or preparations with a
view to use took place.
(3) However, it is not an act of infringement of
a patent to make, use, offer to sell, or sell
within the Republic of Rwanda or import
into the Republic of Rwanda a patented
invention solely for uses reasonably related
to the development and submission of
information as required under a domestic
or foreign law governing the manufacture,
construction, use or sale of a product.
113

articles.heading: Duration of protection of patent rights (1) Patent rights are protected for a period of 20 years from the filing date of the
articles.text:
patent application.
(2) In order to maintain the patent in force
an annual fee is paid in advance for
each year, starting from the filing date
of patent application.
(3) The due date of each annual fee is the
same date as the filing date of
application.
(4) However, a grace period of six months
is granted for payment of the patent
maintenance annual fee after the
deadline. Payment made during the
grace period are subject to payment of
the prescribed surcharge.
(5) If an annual patent maintenance fee is
not paid, the patent lapses.
114
Section 4: Patent assignment

articles.heading: Modalities for patent assignment (1) A pending patent application or a patent may be assigned to a person
articles.text:
through a written patent assignment
contract signed by both parties.
(2) If there is a co-ownership over a patent,
each of the owners may assign
separately, his or her share in the
patent.
(3) Upon payment of the prescribed fee, a
patent assignee submits a patent
assignment contract signed by both
parties to the competent authority who
records the change in the patent
ownership in the register of patents and
publishes the details.
115
(4) The patent assignment becomes valid
and enforceable if it is recorded in the
register of patents.

articles.heading: Refusal to record a patent assignment contract (1) The competent authority does not record a
articles.text:
patent assignment contract if it considers
that one or more clauses of the patent
assignment contract, or the contract as a
whole, have the intention, effect, or are
likely to have effect of the following:
(a) lessening competition;
(b) restraining trade;
(c) abusing a position of market power
conferred by the patent; or
(d) unduly limiting the dissemination of
technology.
116
(2) Before making a decision, the competent
authority may hear submissions from the
parties to the contract and may seek advice
from the organ in charge of competition
regulation.
(3) A decision to refuse to record the patent
assignment contract can be subject to
appeal before the Appeal Committee
within 30 days from the date of notification
of the decision to the parties to the contract.
(4) A contractual term imposing a limitation or
restriction on the patent assignee that does
not relate to a requirement of this Law and
is not reasonably necessary for the
safeguard of the patent rights is considered
to have anti-competitive effect.

articles.heading: Patent contractual licence (1) A patent owner, through a written contractual agreement signed by both
articles.text:
parties, may grant an exclusive, semiexclusive or nonexclusive licence to
another person authorising that person
117
to engage in at least one of the acts
constituting use of the patented
invention.
(2) Upon payment of the prescribed fee, a
patent licensee submits a copy of the
licence contract to the competent
authority who records the subject
matter of the licence contract in the
register of patents and keeps licence
contract confidential.
(3) The patent licence becomes valid and
enforceable if it is recorded in the
register of patents.

articles.heading: Withdrawal of patent contractual licence The patent contractual licence is withdrawn by the competent authority if in case of
articles.text:
(a) termination of the patent licence
contract by one or both parties;
118
(b) invalidation of the patent by a court.

articles.heading: Refusal to record a patent contractual licence (1) The competent authority does not record a
articles.text:
patent contractual licence if it considers
that one or more clauses of the patent
contractual licence, or the contractual
licence as a whole has anti-competitive
effect.
(2) Before making a decision, the competent
authority may hear submissions from the
parties to the agreement and may seek
advice from the organ in charge of
competition regulation.
(3) A decision to refuse to record the patent
contractual licence can be subject to appeal
before the Appeal Committee within 30
days from the date of notification of the
decision to the contracting parties.
(4) A contractual term imposing a limitation or
restriction on the patent licensee that does
119
not relate to a requirement of this Law and
is not reasonably necessary for the
safeguard of the patent rights is considered
to have anti-competitive effect.

articles.heading: Patent contractual licence clauses likely to have anti-competitive effect (1) The following patent contractual licence
articles.text:
clauses are considered as having anticompetitive effect:
(a) clause that requires the patent
licensee to exclusively grant back
to the licensor a licence in respect
of any subsequent patent which
builds upon or improves the
original licenced patent;
(b) clause that requires the patent
licensee not to oppose, seek
revocation or invalidation of the
grant of a patent;
120
(c) clause that coerces the patent
licensee to acquire a licence in
respect of another industrial
property right as a condition for the
granting of a contractual licence
over the patent;
(d) clause that imposes an obligation
on the patent licensee to pay
unreasonable fee for a patent not yet
used;
(e) clause that imposes an obligation
on the patent licensee to purchase
raw materials, intermediate
products, or equipment from the
patent licensor;
(f) clause that prevents the patent
licensee from exporting the
patented products or products
incorporating the patented
invention, or preventing the export
without payment of an
unreasonable fee to the patent
licensor;
(g) clause that limits in any way the
patent licensee’s opportunities to
121
use the patent on internal or
external markets;
(h) clause that contains a
supplementary obligation which,
by its nature or according to
commercial usage, has no
connection with the subject matter
of the agreement.
(2) An Order of the Minister may determine
other patent contractual licence clauses that
are considered as having anti-competitive
effect.
Section 5: Non-contractual patent licence
Subsection One: Patent licence as of right

articles.heading: Procedure for granting a patent licence as of right (1) The patent owner, at any time following the grant of a patent, may
articles.text:
submit a written request to the
122
competent authority for recording in
the patent register a notification that a
patent licence as of right is available in
respect of that patent.
(2) The recording of a patent licence as of
right grants a person the right to use the
patented invention subject to
conditions agreed upon between the
patent owner and the person who
applies for the patent licence as of right
and approved by the competent
authority.
(3) If a patent contractual licence has been
previously registered, no recording of a
patent licence as of right is conducted
unless with the consent of the patent
licensee.
(4) Following the recording of a patent
licence as of right, the patent
maintenance annual fee is reduced by
half.
123

articles.heading: Withdrawal of a patent licence as of right (1) The patent owner, at any time following recording of a patent licence
articles.text:
as of right, may request the competent
authority to withdraw the patent
licence as of right.
(2) The competent authority may withdraw
the patent licence as of right if no other
licence has been granted or if all patent
licensees’ consent.
(3) The withdrawal of a patent licence as
of right is done upon payment of a
balance of all the annual maintenance
fees if the recording had never been
made.
Subsection 2: Compulsory licence of patent
124

articles.heading: Application for compulsory licence of patent (1) Upon payment of the prescribed fee, an applicant for compulsory licence of
articles.text:
patent submits a written application to
the Minister for consideration.
(2) The application for a compulsory
licence of patent is accompanied by
proof that the patent owner has
received from the applicant a
contractual licence request, but that the
latter has been unable to obtain such a
licence on reasonable commercial
conditions and within a reasonable
period.

articles.heading: Granting a compulsory licence of patent (1) The Minister may, upon request by the person wishing to be granted a compulsory
articles.text:
licence of patent, after hearing the patent
owner and after consultation with the
competent authority, grant a licence to use
a patented invention without any
authorisation from the owner of rights on
the invention.
125
(2) Grounds for granting a compulsory licence
of patent are the following:
(a) patented invention is not being
industrially or commercially used in
the Republic of Rwanda;
(b) patented invention is being
insufficiently industrially or
commercially used in the Republic of
Rwanda because the patented invention
or a product incorporating the patented
invention is not available through
manufacture or importation:
(i) in a quantity sufficient to meet
domestic demand;
(ii) in a quality reasonably fit for purpose;
(iii) at a reasonable price;
(c) patent owner is exercising his or her
exclusive rights to the patented
invention, or is neglecting to take
measures to prevent a patent licensee
from exercising his or her licenced
rights to the patented invention, in a
126
way that has the purpose, effect or is
likely to have effect of:
(i) lessening competition;
(ii) restraining trade;
(iii) abusing a position of market power
conferred by the patent;
(iv)unduly limiting the dissemination of
technology;
(d) invention claimed in a subsequent
patent cannot be used in the Republic
of Rwanda without infringing the
previous patent.
(3) The applicant for the grant of a
compulsory licence of patent must
indicate that he or she has filed an
application for the licence to use a
patented invention but has not been
able to obtain it.
127

articles.heading: Requirements for application for a compulsory patent licence due to absent or insufficient use
articles.text:
(1) Requirements for application for
compulsory patent licence due to absence
or insufficient use of the patent are the
following:
(a) expiration of a four-year period from
the filing date of the application, or
three years from the date of grant of the
patent; and
(b) ability to commercially or industrially
use the patented invention to meet
domestic demand.
(2) The Minister, upon his/her own motion, on
advice of the competent authority, or at the
request of any interested person, may
declare the patent rights extinct, or
forfeiture of the patent, where the grant of
compulsory patent licence would not have
been sufficient to prevent insufficient use.
128
(3) No proceedings for the forfeiture or
revocation of compulsory licence may be
initiated before the expiration of two years
from the granting of the first compulsory
licence.

articles.heading: Conditions for issuance of compulsory patent licence in case of interdependence of patents The Minister may issue a compulsory patent
articles.text:
licence in case of interdependence of patents
if:
(a) a later invention owned by the
applicant cannot be used without an
earlier invention owned by another
person; and
(b) he later invention represents significant
technical progress and it is of
considerable economic interest
compared to the invention claimed in
the earlier patent.
129

articles.heading: Conditions for using a compulsory licence of patent in case of interdependence of patents A compulsory licence of patent in case of
articles.text:
interdependence of patents is used if the
following conditions are met:
(a) owner of the earlier patent is entitled to
a licence on reasonable terms to use the
later invention;
(b) use of the previous patent granted
under the compulsory licence of patent
can be assigned only with the
assignment of the later patent.

articles.heading: Content of a compulsory licence of patent (1) A compulsory licence of patent specifies the following
articles.text:
(a) its scope of application and function;
130
(b) its duration;
(c) period within which its beneficiary
begins to use the patented invention;
(d) amount of remuneration to be paid to
the patent owner and the conditions of
payment.
(2) The compulsory licence of patent is used
only within the Republic of Rwanda and
cannot be exclusive.

articles.heading: Filing a case against a decision granting a compulsory licence of patent A case against a decision granting the
articles.text:
compulsory licence of patent or any of the
conditions attached to that licence can be filed
with the competent court by an interested
person.
Subsection 3: Ex officio compulsory licence
of patent
131

articles.heading: Conditions for granting ex officio compulsory licence of patent The Minister may decide that, even without the
articles.text:
consent of the patent owner but, taking into
account the economic value of licenced
invention, with compensation to the patent
owner, a State organ or a designated third party
use the patented invention for the following
reasons:
(a) public interests, in particular:
(i) national security;
(ii) public health;
(iii) environment protection.
(b) a decision of a court or the competent
authority has determined that the patent
owner or his or her licensee uses the
patented invention in unfair competitive
manner.
132

articles.heading: Grant of an ex officio compulsory licence of patent (1) Prior to granting an ex officio compulsory licence of patent, the
articles.text:
Minister negotiates with the patent
owner on a patent contractual licence
on reasonable commercial conditions,
and within a reasonable period.
(2) An Order of the Minister determines
the modalities and period within which
an ex officio compulsory licence of
patent is granted.
(3) The use of the invention is limited to
the purpose for which the ex officio
compulsory licence of patent has been
granted and to supply mainly products
the Rwandan market.

articles.heading: Publication of a decision to grant an ex officio compulsory licence of patent A decision to grant an ex officio compulsory
articles.text:
licence of patent is published in the Official
Gazette of the Republic of Rwanda within 15
133
working days from the date on which the
decision was made.

articles.heading: Amendment or withdrawal of an ex officio compulsory licence (1) At the request of the government agency to
articles.text:
which the ex officio compulsory licence
has been issued, or the third party
authorised to use the patented invention,
the Minister may, after hearing the
interested parties, amend the terms of the
ex officio compulsory licence.
(2) The Minister withdraw the ex officio
compulsory licence after hearing the
interested parties if he or she is satisfied
that:
(a) circumstances which led him or her to
issue the ex officio compulsory licence
have ceased to exist and will most
probably not reoccur;
(b) government agency or third party
authorised by him or her it has not
respected the conditions of the ex
officio compulsory licence.
134

articles.heading: Use of patent owner’s rights in case of grant of ex officio compulsory licence (1) The issuance of an ex officio compulsory
articles.text:
licence does not prevent the patent owner
from:
(a) continuing to use the invention in the
exercise of his or her rights; and
(b) granting the licence.
(2) If the Minister grants an ex officio
compulsory licence to a third party, such a
licence cannot be assigned, sub-licenced,
or otherwise transferred except with the
permission of the Minister.
(3) A case against a decision of the Minister
regarding the grant of the ex officio
compulsory licence may be filed with the
competent court.
Section 6: Regional or International
Application
135

articles.heading: The competent authority as a receiving office for the application (1) The competent authority acts as the
articles.text:
receiving office for a regional or
international application unless
provided otherwise in the Treaty or
notification.
(2) Those authorised to file a regional or an
international application are provided
for in Article 250 of this Law.

articles.heading: The competent authority as a designated office The competent authority acts as the designated
articles.text:
office with regard to regional or international
application where Rwanda is referred to in
respect of granting domestically the patent
under the Patent Cooperation Treaty and
Harare Protocol.

articles.heading: Entering the national phase for the application (1) In case of an international application
articles.text:
136
stating Rwanda as designated country
under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the
applicant may file his or her application at
a national level after:
(a) submission of the application to the
competent authority;
(b) payment of the prescribed fee to the
competent authority;
(c) submission of an international
application translated into the required
language, where necessary.
(2) If the applicant fails to comply with the
provisions of Subparagraphs (b) and (c) of
Paragraph (1) of this Article, the competent
authority invites him or her to address such
compliance issues within the period of 30
days failing which the application is
considered as abandoned.
137

articles.heading: Effect of a regional or international application of patent A regional or international application stating
articles.text:
Rwanda as designated country has the same
effects as the patent application at the
national level if the it is indicated as such in a
regional or international application but the
patent granted regionally or internationally
has the same effects as the patent which is
granted in the Republic of Rwanda unless the
competent authority notifies the international
or regional bureau in respect of such
application that the claims are excluded from
patented property in the Republic of Rwanda.

articles.heading: Processing of a regional or an international application for a patent stating Rwanda as a designated country
articles.text:
(1) The Competent Authority does not
commence the processing of a regional
or an international application for a
patent before the expiration of the time
138
limit for the processing of international
application provided under the Patent
Cooperation Treaty and Harare
Protocol.
(2) However, the applicant may request the
competent authority to process the
application without being bound by the
time limit specified by international or
regional conventions upon payment of
a prescribed fee.
(3) Where the application is filed in a
language other than the official
languages, the applicant submits a
translation of the application into one
of the official languages.
(4) If the applicant does not comply with
the provisions of Paragraph (3) of this
Article, the application is considered to
be abandoned.
139

articles.heading: The filing date of application for international application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty
articles.text:
The filing date of application for international
application stating Rwanda as designated
country and which is filed under the Patent
Cooperation Treaty is the date on which the
application for patent is filed in accordance
with this Law.

articles.heading: Reinstatement of rights on the application considered as abandoned (1) If an international or a regional
articles.text:
application for a patent is considered as
abandoned, the applicant may request
the competent authority to have his or
her rights reinstated if he or she can
show valid reasons.
(2) The Competent Authority does not,
while considering an international or a
regional application for a patent, refuse
an application without providing the
applicant with an opportunity to be
heard within 30 days from the date on
which the regional or international
140
application for a patent is considered as
abandoned.

articles.heading: Reinstatement of right of priority for a regional or an international application (1) An applicant may, if he has a regional
articles.text:
or an international application filing
date, which is later than the date on
which the priority period expired but
within the period of two months from
that date request that the right of
priority of the earlier application be
reinstated.
(2) he Competent Authority reinstates the
right of priority with respect to regional
or international application if it finds
that the failure to file the regional or
international application within the
priority period:
(a) was unintentional; or
(b) occurred despite the fact that the
applicant had taken the required due
care to secure the priority right.
141
(3) The Competent Authority does not
refuse regional or an international
application without providing the
applicant with an opportunity to be
heard within 30 days from the date he
or she was notified thereof.

articles.heading: Processing of a regional or an international application (1) If the applicant fulfils all the
articles.text:
requirements, the competent authority
examines the regional or international
application in accordance with the
provision of matters excluded from
patentability and notify to the regional
and international office on the decision
of approving or rejecting the
application.
(2) If the applicant has filed an express
request for early commencement of the
processing without following
international treaties, his or her
application undergoes the ordinary
national processing phase.
142

CHAPTER IV: PROTECTION OF
INDUSTRIAL DESIGN
Section One: Industrial design protection
requirements

articles.heading: Industrial design eligible for registration (1) An industrial design assembling lines colours or shapes of industrial or craft
articles.text:
product are considered to be a model for
the manufacture of an industrial or craft
product making up an industrial design.
(2) An industrial design may be registered if it
is new.
(3) The registration of an industrial design
does not extend to parts of industrial design
156
which are used only to obtain a technical
result.

articles.heading: Claim and abstract of the industrial design Matters relating to claims and abstract of industrial design are handled in the same way
articles.text:
as provided respectively in Articles 14 and 15
of this Law.

articles.heading: Industrial design excluded from registration An industrial design contrary to public order or
articles.text: morality cannot be registered.

articles.heading: Novelty of an industrial design (1) Industrial design is new if it is not anticipated by the prior art
articles.text:
157
(2) The assessment of prior art takes into
consideration the disclosure of an
industrial design that has been
disclosed anywhere in the world by
publication in tangible form, by oral
disclosure, by use or in any other way
prior to the filing date or, where
applicable, the priority date of the
creation of an industrial design.
(3) However, the disclosure of the
industrial design is not considered
when determining the novelty of an
industrial design if:
(a) it occurs within six months preceding
the filing date of an industrial design
registration application; or it occurs
before the priority date of the industrial
design registration application where
applicable;
(b) it has resulted directly or indirectly
from acts committed by the applicant
for industrial design registration;
158
(c) it has resulted from an abuse
committed by a third party with regard
to the applicant for industrial design
registration or the rightful predecessor.
Section 2: Application for registration of an
industrial design

articles.heading: Filing the application for registration of an industrial design (1) An application for registration of
articles.text:
industrial design is filed with the
competent authority.
(2) An application for registration of an
industrial design is made by filling in a
relevant form prescribed by the
competent authority.
(3) The application for registration of an
industrial design may contain up to 100
159
industrial designs, provided that the
products to which the industrial
designs apply are part of the same class
of product of the international
classification for industrial designs.
(4) The application for registration of
industrial designs may be accompanied
by a specimen of an item incorporating
the industrial designs if that application
concerns a two-dimensional industrial
design.
(5) he application file for registration of an
industrial design is subject to payment
of the prescribed fee regardless of the
number of industrial designs the
application file contains.
(6) The request for registration of an
industrial design can include a request
that once registered, the publication of
the industrial designs be suspended for
a maximum period of 12 months from
the application filing date or, where
priority is claimed, from its priority
date.
160

articles.heading: Setting the filing date of application for registration of an industrial design (1) The competent authority sets, as the
articles.text:
filing date of the application, the date
of receipt of the application, in
accordance with the provisions of

articles.heading: Examination of the application for the registration of an industrial design Before examining the substance of the
articles.text:
application for the registration of an industrial
design, the competent authority determines
whether the requirements for registration of
industrial design provided respectively in
Articles 109 and 110 of this Law are complied.

articles.heading: Examination of the substance of application for registration of an industrial design During examination of the substance of
articles.text:
application for registration of an industrial

report and any international
preliminary examination report
established in accordance with the
Harare Protocol or any other
international convention to which
162
Rwanda is party in relation to the

Rwanda;
(b) results of any search, examination
report or decision provided under this
Law;
(c) results of any search or examination
report which was carried out by a
specialised agency of the Republic of
Rwanda or a foreign organisation
conducting search and examination.

articles.heading: Publication of application for registration of an industrial design (1) The competent authority publishes
articles.text:
application for registration of an
industrial design in the of the Republic of Rwanda after three
months from the date on which the
requirements are met.
(2) The publication of application for
registration of an industrial design
indicates the following information:
163
(a) application number;

five drawings, photograph or other
appropriate graphic representation of
the item incorporating the industrial
design;
(g) description of the products for which
the industrial design is intended to be
used.

164
design are handled in the same way as

165
Section 4: Registration of an industrial
design, its publication and invalidation

articles.heading: Grant or refusal of registration of an industrial design Matters relating to the grant or refusal of
articles.text:
registration of an industrial design are handled
in the same way as provided in Article 31 of

articles.heading: Publication of registration of an industrial design Matters relating to publication of registration
articles.text:
of an industrial design are handled in the same

articles.heading: Suspension of publication of registration of an industrial design (1) If a request for suspension of publication of
articles.text:
166
registration of an industrial design has been
made in accordance with the provisions of
Paragraph (6) of Article 109 of this Law,
the file relating to the registration of an
industrial design is not open for public
inspection for a period of suspension
requested, and the competent authority
only publishes:
(a) reference to the suspension of
publication of registration of an
industrial design;
(b) identity of the owner of the registered
industrial design;
(c) filing date of the application;
(d) duration of the period for which
suspension has been requested.
(2) If the period of suspension expires, the
competent authority makes available to the
public, copies of the registered industrial
design upon payment of prescribed fee.
167

articles.heading: Invalidation of registration of an industrial design (1) An interested person may request the
articles.text:
competent court to invalidate the
registration of an industrial design if such
a person provides one the following
grounds:
(a) the industrial design is not new;
(b) the industrial design is excluded from
registration;
(c) the registration owner is not the creator
or did not have the right to apply for the
registration of the industrial designs.
(2) The competent court may, declare that an
industrial design be registered on the
person who requested for invalidation of
the registration if that person proves to be
the creator of that industrial design and has
requested the registration be made on his or
her name.
168
(3) The interested person notifies the
competent authority of the final decision of
the court to invalidate the registration of an
industrial design so as:
(a) to record the court decision in the
register of industrial designs;
(b) to mark the industrial design as
invalidated in the register of industrial
designs;
(c) to publish a notice referring to the
decision of the court within 30 days
from the date of notification.
169

articles.heading: Effect of invalidation of an industrial design (1) If the grounds for invalidation of the registration of an industrial design are
articles.text:
established with respect to a part of the
concerned industrial design, only the
corresponding claim is invalidated.
(2) The industrial design, claim or part of a
claim that has been invalidated is
deemed null and void as from the date
of issuance of the certificate of
registration.

articles.heading: Transfer of registration of an industrial design Matters relating to transfer of registration of an
articles.text:
industrial design are handled in the same way
as provided in Paragraph (2) Article 34 of this
Law.
170
Section 5: Rights conferred by registration
of an industrial design and their duration

articles.heading: Rights conferred by registration of an industrial design (1) The registration of an industrial design
articles.text:
confers on the owner the exclusive
rights to use the registered industrial
design in the Republic of Rwanda.
(2) The registration confers on the owner
the exclusive rights to stop the use of
the registered industrial design, by any
person without authorisation by the
owner.
(3) The use of a registered industrial
design means at least one of the
following acts:
(a) making, importing, offering for sale,
selling or using a product incorporating
the registered industrial design;
171
(b) stocking a product incorporating the
registered industrial design for the
purposes of offering it for sale, selling
or using it.
(4) The use of a registered industrial
design does not include acts relating to
products which have been put lawfully
on the market in the Republic of
Rwanda by the registered owner or any
other person authorised by him or her.

articles.heading: Civil proceedings against infringement of registration of an industrial design Matters relating to civil proceedings against
articles.text:
infringement of registration of an industrial
design are handled in the same way as
provided in Article 37 of this Law.
172

articles.heading: Joint ownership of an industrial design (1) If two or more persons have created an industrial design together, the right to
articles.text:
apply for registration or a certificate
belongs to each of them.
(2) In the absence of an agreement
between the parties, co-owners of an
industrial design may separately
transfer their shares in the application
and prevent any person from using
their application, but may only jointly
licence any third person to do any of
the acts referred to in this Law.

articles.heading: Naming the creator of industrial design Matters relating to Naming the creator of industrial design are handled in the same way
articles.text:
as provided in Article 39 of this Law.
173

articles.heading: Duration of protection of the registered industrial design (1) A registered industrial design is
articles.text:
protected for a period of 15 years from
the filing date of the application for
registration.
(2) In order to maintain industrial design
rights, the owner of a registered
industrial design pays a prescribed
maintenance fee.
(3) The first payment is made five years
after the filing date of the application
for registration of an industrial design
and the second payment is made ten
years after the filing date of the
application.
(4) A grace period of six months is granted
for payment of maintenance fee of
industrial design rights after the
deadline for payment.
174
(5) The payment made during the grace
period is subject to payment of the
prescribed surcharge.
(6) If the industrial design rights
maintenance fee is not paid, such rights
lapse.
Section 6: Regional and international
registration of an industrial design

articles.heading: Regional and international registration and processing of an industrial design Matters relating to the competent authority as
articles.text:
a receiving office for application, the
competent authority as designated office, a
filing date of an international application,
industrial design excluded from registration,
examination of the substance of application for
registration of industrial design and
verification, approval and transmission of a
regional or international application for
registration of industrial design are handled in
the same way as provided respectively in
175
Articles 62, 63, 67, 107, 112 and 225 of this
Law.

registration of an industrial design

of certificate of registration of an industrial

certificate of registration of an industrial

articles.heading: Withdrawal of contractual licence of certificate of registration of an industrial design Matters relating to withdrawal of contractual
articles.text:
licence of certificate of registration of an

articles.heading: Refusal to record contractual licence of certificate of registration of an industrial design

Matters relating to refusal to record contractual

compulsory licence for an industrial design are

licence for an industrial design are handled in
