CHAPTER V: PROTECTION OF A
LAYOUT-DESIGN OF INTEGRATED
CIRCUIT
Section One: Requirements for protection
of a layout-design of integrated circuit

articles.heading: Layout-design of integrated circuit eligible for protection The layout-design of integrated circuit is
articles.text:
protected if:
(a) it is original;
(b) it has not been previously exploited for
commercial purposes anywhere in the
world; or
(c) it has been previously exploited for
commercial purposes anywhere in the
world within two years.
181

articles.heading: Originality of a layout-design of integrated circuit (1) A layout-design of integrated circuit is
articles.text:
considered to be original if:
(a) it is the result of the intellectual effort
of its creator;
(b) at the time it is created, it is not known
among the creators of layout-designs
and the manufacturers of integrated
circuits.
(2) A layout-design of integrated circuit which
consists of a combination of elements and
interconnections that are common is
protected only if the combination, taken as
a whole, is original.
182

articles.heading: Claims of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the novelty of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit are handled in the
articles.text:
same way as provided in Article 14 of this
Law.

articles.heading: Abstract of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the abstract of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit are handled in the
articles.text:
same way as provided in Article 15 of this
Law.
Section 2: Application for registration of a
layout-design of integrated circuit
183

articles.heading: Filing the application for registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the filing the application for
articles.text:
registration of a layout-design of integrated
circuit are handled in the same way as provided
in Article 9 of this Law.

articles.heading: Setting the filing date of application for registration of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit
articles.text:
(1) The competent authority sets as the
filing date of the application for
registration of a layout-design of
integrated circuit, the date of receipt of
the application in accordance with the
provisions of Article 9 of this Law.
(2) However, if the requirements are not
met, the competent authority invites the
applicant to remedy the irregularity
within 14 days from the date the
invitation is sent.
184
(3) If the applicant remedies the
irregularity, the application filing date
is the date of receipt of such a remedy.
(4) If the applicant does not remedy the
irregularity, the application is deemed
withdrawn.
Section 3: Examination, publication and
opposition of application for registration of
a layout-design of integrated circuit

articles.heading: Examination of application for registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit (1) Before registration of a layout-design of
articles.text:
integrated circuit the competent authority
determines whether the application meets
the requirements provided for in Article 9
of this Law are complied.
(2) If the requirements are not met, the
competent authority notifies the applicant
of irregularities he or she has to remedy
185
within 30 days from the date of the
notification.
(3) If the applicant does not remedy the
irregularity within the period referred to in
Paragraph (2) of this Article, the
application is deemed abandoned.

articles.heading: Publication for application of registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit (1) The competent authority publishes the
Opposition to the registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to opposition to the
articles.text:
187
registration of a layout-design of integrated
circuit are handled in the same way as provided
in Paragraph (1) of Article 29 of this Law.

articles.heading: Procedure for opposition to the registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the procedure for
articles.text:
opposition to the registration of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit are handled in the
same way as provided in Paragraph (2) of

articles.heading: Appeal against the decision on opposition to the registration of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit
articles.text:
Matters relating to appeal against the decision
on opposition to the registration of layoutdesigns of integrated circuit are handled in the
same way as provided in Article 30 of this
Law.
188

articles.heading: Rights of the applicant for registration of a layout-design during publication period (1) After an application is published and
articles.text:
until the registration of layout-designs,
the applicant has the same privileges
and rights as he or she would have if
the layout-design of integrated circuit
was registered.
(2) However, if an application for
registration of a layout-design of
integrated circuit is successfully
opposed, the privileges and rights are
null as from the filing date of the
application.
Section 4: Registration of a layout-design,
its publication and invalidation
189

articles.heading: Registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the registration of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit are handled in the
articles.text:
same way as provided in Article 31 of this
Law.

articles.heading: Publication of registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the publication of
articles.text:
registration of a layout-design of integrated
circuit are handled in the same way as provided
in Article 32 of this Law.

articles.heading: Invalidation of registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit (1) An interested person may request the
articles.text:
competent court to invalidate the
registration of a layout-design of integrated
190
circuit if such a person provides one the
following grounds:
(a) a layout-design of integrated circuit is
not original;
(b) the owner of the registered layoutdesign of integrated circuit is not the
creator or did not have the right to
apply for the registration of the layoutdesign of integrated circuit.
(c) The layout-design of integrated circuit
has been exploited for commercial
purposes anywhere in the world for
over two years.
(2) The competent court may declare that a
layout-design of integrated circuit be
registered on the person who requested for
invalidation of the registration if that
person proves to be the creator of that
layout-design of integrated circuit and has
191
requested the registration be made on his or
her name.
(3) The interested person notifies the
competent authority of the final decision of
the court to invalidate the registration of a
layout-design of integrated circuit so as:
(a) to record the court decision in the
register of layout-designs of integrated
circuit;
(b) to mark the layout-design of integrated
circuit as invalidated in the register of
layout-designs of integrated circuit;
(c) to publish a notice referring to the
decision of the court within 30 days
from the date of notification.
192

articles.heading: Effects of invalidating registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the effect of invalidating
articles.text:
registration of a layout-design of integrated
circuit are handled in the same way as provided
in Article 35 of this Law.

articles.heading: Transfer of registration of layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to the transfer of registration
articles.text:
of layout-design of integrated circuit are
handled in the same way as provided in
Paragraph (2) Article 34 of this Law.
Section 5: Protection of rights conferred by
registration of a layout-design and its
duration
193

articles.heading: Rights conferred by registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit (1) The registration of a layout-design of
articles.text:
integrated circuit confers on the owner
the exclusive rights to exploit the
registered layout-design of integrated
circuit in the Republic of Rwanda.
(2) The use of a registered layout-design of
integrated circuit means at least one of
the following acts:
(a) reproducing, either by incorporation in
an integrated circuit or otherwise, the
whole of the protected layout-design of
integrated circuit or any part thereof,
except the act of reproducing a part
which does not satisfy the requirement
of originality;
(b) importing, selling or otherwise
distributing, for commercial purposes,
194
the protected layout-design of
integrated circuit, an integrated circuit
in which the protected layout-design is
incorporated or an article incorporating
such an integrated circuit, insofar as it
continues to contain a layout-design of
integrated circuit unlawfully
reproduced.
(3) The use of a registered layout-design of
integrated circuit does not include acts
relating to products which have been
put lawfully on the market in the
Republic of Rwanda by the registered
owner or another person authorised by
him or her.
(4) The registration of layout-design of
integrated circuit confers on the owner
the exclusive rights to stop the use of
the registered layout-design of
195
integrated circuit in the Republic of
Rwanda, by any person without
authorisation by the owner, including:
(a) making, importing, offering for sale,
selling a product incorporating the
registered layout-design of integrated
circuit;
(b) stocking a product incorporating the
registered layout-design of integrated
circuit for the purposes of offering it for
sale, selling or using it.

articles.heading: Civil proceedings against infringement of registration of layoutdesign of integrated circuit
articles.text:
Matters relating to civil proceedings against
infringement of registration of layout-design
196
of integrated circuit are handled in the same
way as provided in Article 37 of this Law.

articles.heading: Limitations to the rights on layout-design of integrated circuit The protection granted to a layout-design of
articles.text:
integrated circuit does not extend to:
(a) reproduction of the protected layoutdesign of integrated circuit for private,
non-commercial purposes or for the
sole purpose of evaluation, analysis,
research or education;
(b) incorporation, in an integrated circuit,
of a layout-design of integrated circuit
created on the basis of an analysis or
evaluation and itself exhibiting
originality or the performance of any of
the acts provided under Paragraphs (1)
and (2) of Article 159 of this Law in
respect of that layout-design of
integrated circuit;
197
(c) performance of any of the acts
provided under this Law, as regards an
integrated circuit incorporating a
layout-design of integrated circuit
unlawfully reproduced, or of any
product incorporating such an
integrated circuit, where the person
performing this act, or having it
performed, did not know or had no
valid reason to know, when purchasing
the integrated circuit or the product
incorporating such an integrated
circuit, that it incorporated a layoutdesign of integrated circuit unlawfully
reproduced. However, once this person
has been duly informed, however, that
the layout-design of integrated circuit
has been unlawfully reproduced, he or
she may perform any of the
aforementioned acts relating only to
the stocks held or which he or she had
ordered prior to being thus informed,
and pays the owner a sum equivalent to
the reasonable fee which could be
demanded under a licence freely
negotiated for such a layout-design of
integrated circuit;
198
(d) performance of any of the acts
provided under this Law, where the act
is performed in relation to an original
identical layout-design of integrated
circuit which has been created
independently by a third party.

articles.heading: Joint ownership of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit (1) If two or more persons have made a
articles.text:
layout-design of integrated circuit
together, the right to apply for
registration or a certificate belongs to
each of them.
199
(2) In the absence of an agreement
between the parties, co-owners of a
layout-design of integrated circuit may
separately transfer their shares in the
application and prevent any person
from using their application, but may
only jointly licence any third person to
do any of the acts referred to in this
Law.

articles.heading: Extinction of rights for insufficient exploitation of a layout-design of integrated circuit
articles.text:
(1) The Minister may declare extinction of
rights on a registered layout-design of
integrated circuit if it is being
insufficiently exploited in the Republic
of Rwanda.
(2) In determining whether the registered
layout-design of integrated circuit is
being insufficiently exploited, the
Minister considers whether the protected
layout-design of integrated circuit, an
200
integrated circuit in which the protected
layout-design of integrated circuit is
incorporated or an article incorporating
such an integrated circuit is available in
the Republic of Rwanda:
(a) at an appropriate quality and safety
standard;
(b) in a sufficient quantity to meet
domestic demand;
(c) at a price that is reasonable in all
circumstances.

articles.heading: Authorisation of parallel imports for a layout-design of integrated circuit (1) After declaring extinction of rights of a
articles.text:
registered layout-design of integrated
circuit, the Minister authorises another
person to import the protected layoutdesign of integrated circuit, an integrated
201
circuit in which the protected layoutdesign of integrated circuit is incorporated
or a product incorporating such an
integrated circuit.
(2) The Minister may attach additional
conditions to the authorisation of parallel
imports, relating to the quantity, quality,
and price of the products to be imported,
and any other condition the Minister
considers necessary in the circumstances.
(3) In determining the territory from which
parallel imports is authorised, the Minister
considers the following:
(a) whether the protected layout-design of
integrated circuit, an integrated circuit
in which the protected layout-design of
integrated circuit is incorporated or the
product incorporating the integrated
circuit has been put in the channels of
commerce in the territory by the owner
of the registered layout-design of
202
integrated circuit or by a person
authorised by him or her;
(b) whether the registered layout-design of
integrated circuit protecting the
product is valid in the territory from
which it is to be imported and is owned
by the same person who owns the
certificate of registration of layoutdesign of integrated circuit in the
Republic of Rwanda or by a person
under his or her control.
(4) The Minister cancels the authorization, if
the importer of the product does not
comply with the conditions attached to the
authorisation.
203

articles.heading: Duration for protection of a registered layout-design of integrated circuit (1) The protection granted to a layout-design
articles.text:
of integrated circuit takes effect from:
(a) the date of first exploitation of the
layout-design of integrated circuit,
anywhere in the world, by the owner of
the certificate of registration or with his
or her authorisation, provided that an
application for protection is filed by the
owner with the competent authority of
his or her residence, within two years
from the date of first exploitation;
(b) the date on which the application for
registration of the layout-design of
integrated circuit was filed by the
owner, if the layout-design of
integrated circuit has not been
previously exploited for commercial
purposes anywhere in the world.
204
(2) A registered layout-design of integrated
circuit is protected for a period of ten years
from the date of first exploitation, or from
the filing date whichever is earlier.

articles.heading: Maintenance of the certificate of registration of a layout-design of integrated circuit (1) In order to maintain the certificate of
articles.text:
registration of a layout-design of integrated
circuit, the owner of a registered layoutdesign of integrated circuit pays
maintenance fee to the competent
authority.
(2) The payment is made five years from the
date of first exploitation of the certificate
of registration of a layout-design of
integrated circuit, or from the filing date of
the application whichever is earlier.
205
(3) A grace period of six months is granted for
payment of maintenance fee of the
registered layout-design of integrated
circuit after the deadline.
(4) The payment made during the grace period
is subject to payment of the prescribed
surcharge.
(5) If the fee for the maintenance of the
certificate of registration of a layout-design
of integrated circuit is not paid, the
protection of the registered layout-design
of integrated circuit irrevocably lapses.
Section 6: Assignment of a layout-design of
integrated circuit
206
Article167: Modalities for layout-design of
integrated circuit assignment and refusal to
record a layout-design of integrated circuit
assignment contract
Matters relating to modalities for layoutdesign of integrated circuit assignment and
refusal to record a layout-design of integrated
circuit assignment contract are handled in the
same way as provided respectively in Articles
42 and 43 of this Law.
Section 7: Licence of a layout-design of
integrated circuit

articles.heading: Contractual licence of a layoutdesign of integrated circuit Matters relating to contractual licence of a
articles.text:
layout-design of integrated circuit
handled in the same way as provided in Article
44 of this Law.
207

articles.heading: Withdrawal of contractual licence of a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to withdrawal of contractual
articles.text:
licence of layout-design of integrated circuit
are handled in the same way as provided in

articles.text:
contract on a layout-design of integrated

in Article 46 of this Law.
208

articles.text:
Matters relating to clauses of the contract of
layout-design of integrated circuit that are
likely to have anti-competitive effect are
handled in the same way as provided in Article
47 of this Law.
Section 8: Compulsory licence on a layoutdesign of integrated circuit

articles.heading: Application for a compulsory licence on a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to application for a
articles.text:
compulsory licence on a layout-design of
integrated circuit are handled in the same way
as provided in Article 50 of this Law.
209

articles.heading: Granting a compulsory licence on a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to granting a compulsory
articles.text:
licence on a layout-design of integrated circuit
are handled in the same way as provided in

articles.heading: Requirements for the application for a compulsory licence on a layout-design of integrated circuit
articles.text:
Matters relating to requirements for the
application for a compulsory licence on a
layout-design of integrated circuit are handled
in the same way as provided in Article 52 of
this Law.
210

articles.heading: Procedure for granting a compulsory licence on a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to procedure for granting a
articles.text:
compulsory licence on a layout-design of
integrated circuit are handled in the same way
as provided in Paragraph (1) of Article 50 of
this Law.

articles.heading: Content of a compulsory licence on a layout-design of integrated circuit Matters relating to content of a compulsory
articles.text:
licence on a layout-design of integrated circuit
are handled in the same way as provided in

articles.heading: Filing a case against a decision granting a compulsory licence on a layoutdesign of integrated circuit
articles.text:
Matters relating to filing a case against a
decision granting a compulsory licence on a
layout-design of integrated circuit are handled
in the same way as provided in Article 56 of
this Law.

articles.heading: Conditions for granting of an ex officio compulsory licence on a layoutdesign of integrated circuit
articles.text:
Matters reating to conditions for granting of an
ex officio compulsory licence on a layoutdesign of integrated circuit are handled in the
same way as provided in Article 57 of this
Law.
212

articles.heading: Application and grant of an ex officio compulsory licence on a layoutdesign of integrated circuit
articles.text:
(1) The application for an ex officio
compulsory licence on a layout-design of
integrated circuit is addressed to the
Minister and accompanied by proof that
the owner of certificate of registration of
the layout-design of integrated circuit has
received from the applicant, a contractual
licence request, but that the latter has been
unable to obtain the licence on reasonable
commercial conditions and within a
reasonable period.
(2) The provisions of Paragraph (1) of this
Article does not apply if an ex officio
compulsory licence is granted for the
following reasons:
(a) in a state of emergency;
(b) in the effective use of the layout-design
of integrated circuit for public non
213
commercial interests;
(c) in case of correction of acts of unfair
competition.
(3) If an ex officio compulsory licence was
granted in accordance with the provisions
of Paragraph (2) of this Article, the owner
of the certificate of registration of the
layout-design of integrated circuit is
notified of the decision of Government
within 30 days from the date on which it
was taken.
(4) The exploitation of the layout-design of
integrated circuit is limited to the purposes
for which the licence has been granted and
is subject to payment to the owner or his or
her rightful claimant of appropriate
remuneration, taking into account the
economic value of the decision of
Government, or if the decision has been
taken by a judicial organ or by a competent
authority, considering the need to correct
anticompetitive practices.
214
(5) Subject to the provisions of Paragraph (2)
of this Article, the decision of Government
is taken after the owner of the certificate of
registration of the layout-design of
integrated circuit and any interested person
have been heard by the competent
authority, if they so wish.
(6) In accordance with provisions of Article
178 of this Law, the effective exploitation
of the layout-design of integrated circuit by
the State organ or the third party appointed
by the Government must aim at supplying
the Rwandan market, except if the licence
was granted with an intention of correcting
acts of unfair competition.
(7) An ex officio compulsory licence for the
use of the layout-design of integrated
circuit is only authorised for public noncommercial interests or for the correction
of acts of unfair competition.
215

articles.text:
Matters relating to amendment or withdrawal
of an ex officio compulsory licence on a

articles.text:
Matters relating to the use of rights in case ex
officio compulsory licence on a layout-design
of integrated circuit has been granted are
handled in the same way as provided in Article
61 of this Law.
216
CHAPTER VI: PROTECTION OF
MARK, COLLECTIVE MARK,
CERTIFICATION MARK AND TRADE
NAME
Section One: Mark
Subsection one: Protected mark

articles.heading: Mark eligible for registration (1) A mark eligible for registration is a sign or a combination of signs, capable of
articles.text:
distinguishing the goods or services of
one person from those of other persons.
(2) The following signs are eligible for
registration as a mark:
(a) words, proper names, letters, figures
and abbreviations;
(b) figurative elements including:
(i) designs;
(ii) packaging;
217
(iii)product forms; or
(iv)shapes.
(c) colours or combinations of colours;
(d) any combination of the above signs.

articles.heading: Requirements for registration of a mark (1) A mark is registered if
articles.text:
(a) it is distinctive;
(b) it is not imitative;
(c) it is not confusing;
(d) it is not descriptive.
(2) However, a mark cannot be registered
if the application was made in bad faith
or if the application is an act of unfair
competition.
(3) A mark eligible for registration may
include elements which are not
protected, unless they decrease the
218
distinctive characteristics of the mark
or infringe the rights of other persons.

articles.heading: Distinctive mark (1) A mark is distinctive if it is inherently capable of distinguishing the goods or
articles.text:
services of one person from those of
another person.
(2) However, the competent authority can
decide whether a mark which does not
meet the requirements referred to in
Paragraph (1) of this article has
acquired distinctiveness through
continuous use.

articles.heading: Imitative mark (1) A mark is imitative if
articles.text:
(a) it is identical with, or confusingly
similar to, or constitutes a
translation of a mark or a trade
name which is well-known in the
Republic of Rwanda for identical or
similar goods or services of another
person;
219
(b) it is identical with, or confusingly
similar to, or constitutes a
translation of a mark or a trade
name which is well-known in the
Republic of Rwanda for goods or
services which are not identical or
similar to those in respect of which
registration is applied for, if:
(i) the use of the mark of the
applicant in relation to goods or
services indicates a connection
between those goods or services
and the owner of the well-known
mark;
(ii) the interests of the owner of the
well-known mark are likely to be
damaged by such use;
(c) it is identical to a mark belonging to
another person and which is already
registered, or with an earlier filing
date of application or priority date
for:
(i) same goods or services;
220
(ii) similar goods or services, and its
use is likely to mislead or
confuse; or
(d) it is similar to a mark belonging to
another person and which is already
registered, or with an earlier filing
date of application or priority date
in respect of the same or similar
goods or services, and its use is
likely to mislead or confuse.
(2) determining whether a mark is wellknown, consideration is given to the
degree of recognition of the mark in the
relevant sector of the public in the
Republic of Rwanda including the degree
of recognition arising from the
advertising of the mark.

articles.heading: Confusing mark (1) A mark is confusing if it is likely to mislead consumers, the public or traders, especially as regards to
Descriptive mark A mark is descriptive if it contains among its components, words or expressions which
articles.text:
(a) serve only to designate the kind,
quality, quantity, intended purpose,
value, geographical origin, time of
(
222
production of goods or of rendering of
services, or other fundamental
characteristics of goods or services;
(b) are in common use by consumers in
relation to the goods or services in
respect of which registration of the
mark is applied for;
(c) are common technical terms used in the
relevant field of the goods and services
in respect of which registration of the
mark is applied for.

articles.heading: Application for registration of a mark made in bad faith A mark is not registered if the application is
articles.text:
made in bad faith, or if the registration of a
mark has the effect, or likely to have effect of:
(a) lessening competition;
(b) restraining trade;
(c) abusing a position of market power or
dominance conferred by the mark.
223

articles.heading: Mark excluded from registration and use A mark is excluded from registration and use, if
articles.text:
(a) it is contrary to public order and to
morality;
(b) it reproduces, imitates or contains
among its features armorial bearings,
flags or other emblems, a name or
abbreviation or initials of the name,
official sign or hallmark and guarantee
of a State or intergovernmental
organisation set up by an international
convention, unless authorisation is
given by that State or that
intergovernmental organisation.
Subsection 2: Application for registration of
a mark

articles.heading: of this Law, the competent authority examines the substance of the application in accordance with the
articles.text:
provisions of Articles 183 and 189 of this
Law, in order for a mark to be registered.
(2) The competent authority may require the
applicant to disclaim an unregistrable
component of a mark otherwise registrable.
(3) An applicant may voluntarily disclaim a
component of a mark referred to in
Paragraph (2) of this Article sought to be
registered.
(4) If the application does not meet the
requirements, the competent authority
rejects the application for registration of a
mark and informs in writing the applicant
within 14 days from the date on which the
decision was made.
226

articles.heading: Setting the filing date of the application for registration of a mark (1) The competent authority sets as the
articles.text:
filing date of application for
registration of a mark, the date of
receipt of the application, in
accordance with the provisions of

articles.heading: Examination of the substance of application for registration of a mark (1) If the application for registration of a mark
articles.text: meets the requirements provided for by

articles.heading: Publication of application of registration of a mark (1) The competent authority publishes the
Opposition to the registration of a mark An interested person may oppose the registration of a mark by filling the form
Procedure for opposition to the registration of a mark (1) The competent authority gives notice
articles.text:
of opposition, within seven days from
the date of receipt of notice of
opposition, to the applicant for
registration of a mark for him or her to
provide explanations on the grounds of
opposition.
(2) The applicant for registration of a mark
provides explanations on the grounds
of opposition within 30 days from the
date on which he or she received the
notice of opposition.
(3) If the applicant for registration of a
mark does not provide explanations on
the grounds of opposition, the
application is considered as
abandoned.
(4) If the applicant for registration of a
mark provides explanations on the
grounds of opposition, the competent
authority transmits a copy of the
response to the opposing party.
(5) After hearing both parties and
examining the relevance of the
opposition, the competent authority
229
decides whether it is appropriate to
register or not a mark within 30 days
from the last day of hearing both
parties.

articles.heading: Appeal against the decision on opposition to the registration of a mark (1) An interested person may appeal against a
articles.text:
decision on opposition to the registration of
a mark, before the Appeal Committee,
within 30 days from the date of notification
of the decision of the competent authority.
(2) An Order of the Minister determines the
composition and functioning of the Appeal
Committee.

articles.heading: Effect of rights during publication period (1) After an application is published and until the registration of a mark, the
articles.text:
applicant has the same privileges and
rights as he or she would have if the
mark were registered.
(2) However, if an application for
registration of a mark is successfully
230
opposed, the privileges and rights are
null as from the date of the application.
Subsection 4: Registration of a mark, its
publication and invalidation

articles.heading: Registration of a mark If the application for registration of a mark meets the requirements, the competent
articles.text:
authority proceeds to the following:
(a) records a certificate of registration of a
mark in the register of marks;
(b) issues to the applicant a certificate of
registration of a mark.

articles.heading: Publication of registration of a mark The competent authority publishes the registration of a mark in the the Republic of Rwanda within 30 days from
articles.text:
the date of registration of a mark.
231

articles.heading: Invalidation of the registration of a mark (1) An interested person may apply to the competent court to invalidate the
articles.text:
registration of a mark if at least one of
the following grounds is established:
(a) mark is not distinctive;
(b) mark is imitative;
(c) mark is likely confusing;
(d) mark is descriptive;
(e) mark was registered in bad faith;
and
(f) application for registration of a
mark is made with the aim of unfair
competition.
(2) The competent court may, declare that
a mark be registered on the person who
requested for invalidation of the
registration if that person proves to be
the right owner of the mark and has
requested the registration be made on
his or her name.
232
(3) The interested person notifies the
competent authority of the final
decision of the court to invalidate the
registration of a mark so as:
(a) to record the court decision in the
register of marks;
(b) to mark the mark as invalidated in
the register of marks;
(c) to publish a notice referring to the
decision of the court within 30 days
from the date of notification.

articles.heading: Effects of invalidating registration of a mark An invalidated registration of a mark is regarded as null from the date of registration of
articles.text:
a mark.
Subsection 5: Protection of rights conferred
by registration of marks and its duration
233

articles.heading: Rights conferred by registration of a mark (1) The registration of a mark confers on the owner the exclusive rights to the use of a
articles.text:
mark on the territory of the Republic of
Rwanda.
(2) The registration of a mark also confers on
the owner the exclusive rights to prevent
any person other than the owner from
using it on the territory of the Republic of
Rwanda, without prior authorization of the
owner.

articles.heading: Civil proceedings against infringement of registration of a mark The owner of a registered mark may initiate
articles.text:
civil proceedings before the competent court
against a person who uses, or facilitates or
procures the use of the registered mark without
his or her consent, or a person who facilitates
or procures the use of a mark which is imitative
of the registered mark of the owner.
234

articles.heading: of this Law, the Minister on own motion, at the request of the competent authority or at the request of
articles.text:
any interested person, has the authority
to declare the rights of the mark
exhausted, and in such a case he/she
shall authorize other persons to import
the product provided with a mark or a
product manufactured directly or
indirectly by means of the registered
mark referred to as “the product” from
the territory of another country when:
(a) the product:
236
(i) is not available on the territory of
Rwanda;
(ii) is available on the territory of
Rwanda but does not meet the
required standards;
(iii)cannot be available in sufficient
quantities to meet the domestic
market;
(iv)has a price which the Minister
considers unfair;
(b) for any other reason of public
interest, including acts of unfair
competition.
(3) The decision shall be taken in
consideration of the following:
(a) the product has been put on market
in the territory from which it will be
imported by the owner of certificate
of the mark or by a person
authorized by him/her;
(b) the certificate of registration of the
mark claiming the product or the
process for its manufacture is in
force in the territory from which the
237
product will be imported and is
owned by the same person who
owns the certificate of registration of
the mark in the Republic of Rwanda
or by a person under his/her control.
(4) If the importer of the product fails to
fulfil the requirements that provoked
the Minister to take such a decision of
declaring the extinction of the mark
rights, the Minister shall, ex officio, or
at the request of the owner of the mark,
cancel the authorization.
(5) The provisions of Paragraph (1) of this
Article shall not apply to the use of the
registered mark with informative
purposes, such as to promote sales or
engage in comparative advertisement,
provided such use is not made in a
manner that deceives the public or
constitutes act of unfair competition.
(6) The Minister in charge of health may
take measures to limit the use of marks
with the purpose of facilitating the
prescription of and the access to
generic pharmaceutical products and
medical devices, or with the purpose of
238
discouraging the public consumption
of drugs that are deemed prejudicial to
health, provided such measures do not
unreasonably cause a detriment to the
capability of the marks in question to
distinguish a certain accepted drug
from any other drug accepted to be
used.

articles.heading: Limitations and exhaustion of rights (1) The rights conferred by a registered mark are not extended to the acts
articles.text:
relating to products or services that
have been put lawfully on market, in
the Republic of Rwanda, by the
registration owner or with his or her
consent.
(2) Without prejudice to the provisions of

articles.heading: Duration of protection of the registered mark and its renewal (1) A registered mark is protected for a
articles.text:
period of 10 years from the filing date
of the application for registration.
(2) The duration of protection of a
registered mark can be indefinitely
renewed for consecutive periods of 10
years each, upon request of the owner
of a registered mark. The renewal of
registration of a mark is subject to
payment of the prescribed fee.
(3) However, a grace period of six months
is granted for the payment of the fee for
renewal of the protection of the
registered mark after the deadline for
payment. The payment made during
239
the grace period is subject to payment
of the prescribed surcharge.
(4) If the fee for renewal of a mark is not
paid, the protection of a registered
mark lapses.
Subsection 6: Assignment of a mark

articles.heading: Procedures for assignment of a mark (1) A registered mark may be assigned to a person through a written mark
articles.text:
assignment contract signed by both
parties.
(2) Upon payment of the prescribed fee, a
mark assignee submits a signed mark
assignment contract to the competent
authority who records in the register of
marks the change in the mark
ownership and publishes the details.
(3) The assignment of a mark becomes
valid and enforceable once it is
recorded in the register of marks.
240

articles.heading: Refusal to record a mark assignment contract The competent authority does not record a mark assignment contract if the assignment is
Mark contractual licence 34
Withdrawal of mark contractual licence The mark contractual licence is withdrawn by the competent authority, in case of
articles.text:
(a) termination of the mark licence
contract by one or both parties;
(b) invalidation of the registration of a
mark.

articles.heading: Refusal to record a mark licence contract (1) The competent authority does not record a mark licence contract if it finds
articles.text:
that such a contract contains one or
more clauses, or the whole contract
constitutes an act of unfair competition,
or the licensing of the mark is likely to
mislead, to deceive or to confuse
consumers with regard to:
(a) geographical origin;
243
(b) quality;
(c) nature;
(d) characteristics;
(e) manufacturing process;
(f) suitability for the use for which it is
intended for on goods or services in
respect of which registration of the
mark is applied for by the applicant.
(2) Before making a decision, the
competent authority can hear
submissions from the parties to the
contract and can seek advice from the
organ in charge of competition
regulation.
(3) A decision to refuse to record the mark
licence can be subject to appeal before
the Appeal Committee within 30 days
from the date of notification of the
decision to both parties.
(4) A contractual term imposing a
limitation or restriction on the mark
licensee that does not relate to a
requirement of this Law and is not
244
reasonably necessary for the safeguard
of the registered mark rights is
considered to have effect of unfair
competition.

articles.heading: Mark licence contract clauses likely to have effect of unfair competition The following types of mark licence contract
articles.text:
clauses create a rebuttable presumption in
favour of unfair competition:
(a) a clause that requires the mark licensee
not to oppose, seek revocation or
invalidation of the registration of a
mark;
(b) a clause that coerces the mark licensee
to acquire a licence in respect of
another industrial property right as a
condition for the granting of a
contractual licence over the registered
mark;
(c) a clause that imposes an obligation on
the mark licensee to pay unreasonable
fees for a mark not yet used;
245
(d) a clause that imposes an obligation on
the mark licensee to purchase raw
materials, intermediate products, or
equipment from the licensor;
(e) a clause that prevents the mark licensee
from exporting goods bearing the mark
or preventing such export without the
payment of an unreasonable fee to the
licensor;
(f) a clause that limits in any way the mark
licensee’s opportunities to sell goods
bearing the mark on internal or external
markets;
(g) a clause that contains a supplementary
obligation which, by its nature or
according to commercial usage, has no
connection with the subject matter of
the contract.
Subsection 8: Collective mark

articles.heading: Collective mark A mark, capable of distinguishing the goods or services of persons who are members of an
articles.text:
association, from goods or services of persons
246
who are not members of such association, for
which the application for registration was
made in the prescribed manner, is registrable
as a collective mark in respect of the goods or
services registered in the name of such an
association.

articles.heading: Application for registration of a collective mark Matters related to the requirements for registration of a collective mark, a collective
articles.text:
mark excluded from registration and use,
setting the filing date of the application for
registration of a collective mark, examination
of the substance of application for registration
of a collective mark, publication of application
of registration of a collective mark, opposition
to the registration of a collective mark,
procedure for opposition to the registration of
a collective mark, appeal against the decision
on opposition to the registration of a collective
mark, effect of rights during publication
period, registration of a collective mark,
publication of registration of a collective mark
and the duration of protection of the registered
collective mark and its renewal are handled in
the same way as provided respectively in
articles 183, 189, 191, 192, 193, 194, 195, 196,
197, 198, 199 and 206 of this Law.
247

articles.heading: Filing of the application for registration of a collective mark (1) An application for registration of a
articles.text:
collective mark is made by filling a
form provided for this purpose, which
is prescribed by the competent
authority.
(2) An application for registration of a
collective mark is accompanied by a
copy of the regulations determining the
conditions of use of a collective mark.
(3) The owner of a registered collective mark
notifies the competent authority of any
change made to those regulations.
(4) The filing of the application is subject to
payment of the prescribed fee.

articles.heading: Rights conferred by registration of a collective mark (1) The registration of a collective mark
articles.text:
confers on members of an association the
exclusive rights to the use of a collective
mark on the territory of the Republic of
Rwanda.
248
(2) However, a registered collective mark
cannot be subject to a licence contract.

articles.heading: Invalidation of the registration of a collective mark (1) An interested person may request the
articles.text:
competent court to invalidate the
registration of a collective mark on at
least one of the following grounds:
(a) only one of the co-owners of a
registered collective mark uses the
mark;
(b) one of the co-owners of a collective
mark allows others to use it in
contravention of the regulations
prescribed by the co-owners of a
collective mark determining the
conditions of use of a collective mark;
(c) one of the co-owners of a collective
mark allowed others to use it, or knew
or ought to have known it was being
used in a manner likely to mislead,
249
deceive or confuse consumers or
traders with regards to:
(i) geographical origin;
(ii) quality;
(iii)nature;
(iv)characteristics;
(v) manufacturing process;
(vi)suitability for the use for which they
are intended of the goods or services
to which the collective mark relates.
Subsection 9 : Certification mark

articles.heading: Certification mark A mark distinguishing goods or services certified by an authorised person in respect of
articles.text:
the geographical origin, material,
manufacturing process, quality, accuracy or
other characteristic from goods or services not
so certified, is registrable as a certification
mark.
250

articles.heading: Application for registration of a certification mark Matters related to the requirements for
articles.text:
registration of a certification mark, a
certification mark excluded from registration
and use, filing of the application for
registration of a certification mark, setting the
filing date of the application for registration of
a certification mark, examination of the
substance of application for registration of a
certification mark, publication of application
of registration of a certification mark,
opposition to the registration of a certification
mark, procedure for opposition to the
registration of a certification mark, appeal
against the decision on opposition to the
registration of a certification mark, effect of
rights during publication period, registration of
a certification mark, publication of registration
of a certification mark and the duration of
protection of the registered certification mark
and its renewal are handled in the same way as
provided respectively in articles 183, 189,
191, 192, 193, 194, 195, 196, 197, 198, 199
and 206 of this Law.

articles.heading: Rights conferred by registration a certification mark (1) The registration of a certification mark
articles.text:
251
confers on the owner the exclusive
rights to the use of a certification mark
on the territory of the Republic of
Rwanda.
(2) Any person who has proved that his or
her products or services comply with
the technical standards and other
conditions of the regulations
determining the conditions of use of a
certification mark can request the right
to use the certification mark in the same
conditions as those established by
those regulations.
(3) However, the owner of a certification
mark cannot use the certification mark
to identify or certify his or her own
products or services.

articles.heading: Invalidation of registration of a certification mark An interested person may request the competent court to invalidate the registration
articles.text:
of a certification mark on at least one of the
following grounds:
(a) only the owner of a registered
certification mark uses the mark;
252
(b) the owner of a certification mark
allows others to use it in contravention
of the regulations prescribed by the coowners of a mark determining the
conditions of use of a certification
mark;
(c) the owner of a certification mark
allowed others to use it, or knew or
ought to have known it was being used
in a manner likely to mislead, deceive
or confuse consumers or traders with
regards to:
(i) geographical origin;
(ii) quality;
(iii)nature;
(iv)characteristics;
(v) manufacturing process;
(vi)suitability for the use for which they
are intended of the goods or services
to which the certification mark
relates.
Section 2: Protection of a trade name and
second-level domain name
253

articles.heading: Use of a trade name and second-level domain name (1) A name or designation may not be used as a trade name or a second-level
articles.text:
domain name if:
(a) its nature or its use is contrary to
public order or morality;
(b) it is likely to mislead any person as
to the nature of the company it
designates;
(c) it is identical or similar to a mark
which is registered or well-known
in the Republic of Rwanda;
(d) it consists of a translation of a
registered or a well-known mark in
the Republic of Rwanda.
(2) Pursuant to the legal provisions
providing for the registration of a trade
name or a second-level domain name,
such name is protected against any
254
unlawful act committed by third party,
be it in the form of a trade name, mark
or collective mark, in the same way as
any use of a similar trade name or a
similar mark likely to mislead the
public.
Section 3: International application and
registration of a mark

articles.heading: of this Law; (b) substance of the international application is consistent with the substance of the basic application
articles.text:
or basic registration.
(2) If the competent authority is satisfied that
the international application meets the
requirements, it submits the application to
the International Bureau and confirms the
date of receipt of the international
application.
(3) If the international application does not
meet the requirements, the competent
authority does not forward it to the
International Bureau, but informs the
applicant.
(4) The certification and submission of an
international application for registration
of a mark to the International Bureau are
subject to payment of the prescribed fee.
257

articles.heading: Basis for an international application for registration of a mark stating Rwanda as the country of origin
articles.text:
An international application for registration of
a mark stating the Republic of Rwanda as the
country of origin is well founded if one of the
following requirements is met:
(a) the applicant has filed a basic
application for registration of a mark in
accordance with this Law, and that
application has been accepted by the
competent authority;
(b) a mark is registered in the Republic of
Rwanda.

articles.heading: Verification, certification and submission of an international application for registration of a mark
articles.text:
(1) If an international application for
registration of a mark is filed, the
competent authority verifies if:
256
(a) Rwanda is considered as the country
of origin in respect of that application
in accordance with the provisions of

articles.heading: Examination of an international application stating Rwanda as a designated country (1) An international application for
articles.text:
registration of a mark stating Rwanda as a
designated country is examined by the
competent authority in accordance with
the provisions of Articles 183 and 189 of
this Law.
(2) If the competent authority finds that an
international application meets the
requirements for the registration of a
mark, the application is published and
subject to opposition in accordance with
the provisions of Articles 193 and 194 of
this Law.
(3) The competent authority takes a decision
on the international application for
registration of a mark within 12 months
from the date of receipt of an international
application for registration of a mark and
notifies the International Bureau of its
decision.
258

articles.heading: Provisional refusal of an international application stating Rwanda as a designated country The competent authority may provisionally
articles.text:
refuse to register an international application
and notifies the applicant thereof through the
International Bureau within 12 months from
the date of receipt of an international
application.
The notification includes the following:
(a) grounds for the decision;
(b) any relevant documentation supporting
the decision;
(c) details of the opposition, where the
application is being refused on the
basis of a successful opposition;
(d) details for how the applicant can seek
review of the decision within three
months from the date of notification of
the provisional refusal of his or her
application.
259

articles.heading: Accepting or rejecting an international application for registration of a mark The competent authority examines
articles.text:
explanations provided by an applicant seeking
a review of the decision and takes a final
decision to reject or accept the application and
notifies the International Bureau.

articles.heading: Effects of not notifying International Bureau decision to accept or reject the registration of a mark
articles.text:
If the competent authority does not notify the
International Bureau of the decision to accept
or reject the registration within 12 months from
the date of receipt of the international
application, the registration is considered
accepted.

articles.heading: Notification of invalidation of the basic registration of a mark to the International Bureau
articles.text:
If, during the period of international
registration of a mark, the basic registration is
invalidated by the court and the invalidation is
no longer subject to appeal, the competent
authority notifies the International Bureau of
the invalidation and indicates the following:
260
(a) the court that pronounced the invalidation
and the date of the judgment;
(b) the number of the international
registration and the name of the holder;
(c) the goods and services affected by the
invalidation.

articles.heading: Effects of rights under an international application (1) A person making an international application under this Law stating
articles.text:
Rwanda as a designated country has the
same rights and remedies as any other
applicant for registration of a mark
under this Law.
(2) An international registration stating
Rwanda as designated country has the
same effects, from the date of the
application of international
registration, as if the application for the
registration of the mark had been filed
directly with the competent authority
under this Law.
261
(3) Any recording made in the
International Register in respect of an
international registration stating
Rwanda as designated country, has the
same effect as if it had been recorded
by the competent authority in the
register of marks under this Law.

articles.heading: Ceasing of effect of the basic application or basic registration If, within five years from the filing date of the
articles.text:
basic application or the date of the basic
registration, one or the other ceases to have
effect, the competent authority informs the
International Bureau thereof.

articles.heading: Effect of a cancelled international application Where, in the event that the international registration is cancelled at the request of the
articles.text:
Office of origin, in respect of all or some of the
goods and services listed in the registration, the
applicant of the international registration may
file an application for the registration of the
same mark as the national application and that
application shall be treated as if it had been
filed on the date of the international
262
registration or on the date of, if the
international registration enjoyed priority,
shall enjoy the same priority, provided that;
(a) such application is filed within three
months from the date on which the
international registration was
cancelled;
(b) the goods and services listed in the
application are the same as those
contained in the international
registration;
(c) such application complies with the
requirements of the application of
registration of a mark provided by
Articles 183 and 190 of this Law.
CHAPITER VII: PROTECTION OF
GEOGRAPHICAL INDICATION
Section One: Requirements for protection
of a geographical indication

articles.heading: Protected geographical indication (1) A geographical indication is protected if
articles.text:
263
(a) it indicates the territory, region or
locality of the country in which the
product originates;
(b) it indicates quality and reputation of
a product or other characteristics
that are essentially attributable to its
geographical origin.
(2) However, a geographical indication is
protected whether registered or not.

articles.heading: Registration of homonymous geographical indications (1) When registering a geographical indication that has another
articles.text:
geographical indication that sounds,
spells or reads alike and which
originate in different places, the
competent authority may impose
conditions on its registration to ensure
that:
(a) homonymous indications are
differentiated from each other;
(b) the public is not confused or misled;
264
(c) all producers concerned are treated
equitably.
(2) Subject to the provisions of Paragraph
(1) of this Article, in the case of
homonymous geographical indications
for wines and spirits, protection is
accorded to each geographical
indication.
(3) An order of the Minister may
determine additional products to those
referred to under Paragraph (2) of this
Article.

articles.heading: Geographical indication excluded from protection A geographical indication cannot be protected
articles.text:
where:
(a) a quality, reputation or other specific
characteristic of the product cannot be
attributed essentially to its geographical
origin;
(b) it is contrary to public order or morality;
265
(c) it is not, or has ceased to be, protected in
its country of origin;
(d) it misleads and makes the public consider
that the products originate from a
different territory;
(e) it is identical with the term customary in
common language in the Republic of
Rwanda as the common name for the
relevant product;
(f) it is prejudicial to a prior mark applied for
or registered in good faith, or acquired
through use in good faith in the Republic
of Rwanda.
Section 2: Application for registration of a
geographical indication

articles.heading: Right to apply for registration of a geographical indication The registration of a geographical indication is
articles.text:
applied for by:
(a) an association of persons who indicate
in their application that they carry out
production activities in the
266
geographical region indicated in the
application;
(b) a legal entity operating in the region
indicated in the application, in respect
to a product indicated in the
application, that carries out a
production activity including
agricultural and handicrafts activities
or any other activity;
(c) a public institution having legal
personality and interest in registering a
geographical indication.

articles.heading: Filing the application for registration of a geographical indication (1) An application for registration of a
articles.text:
geographical indication is made by filling
a form provided for this purpose, which
is prescribed by the competent authority.
(2) The filing of the application is subject to
payment of the prescribed fee.
267

articles.heading: Setting the filing date of the application for registration of a geographical indication (1) The competent authority sets as the
articles.text:
filing date of application for
registration of a geographical
indication, the date of receipt of the
application, in accordance with the
provisions of Article 238 of this Law.
(2) However, if the requirements are not
met, the competent authority informs
the applicant that he or she must
complete the missing elements within
14 days from the day of notification.
(3) If the applicant complies with the
requirements, the date of receipt of the
missing elements is considered as the
filing date.
(4) If the applicant does not comply with
the requirements, the application is
considered as withdrawn.
Section 3: Examination and publication of
registration of a geographical indication
270
(i) the geographical region for which
the geographical indication applies;
(ii) the products to which the
geographical indication applies;
(iii)quality, reputation or other
characteristic of the products.

articles.heading: Examination of the substance of application for registration of a geographical indication
Publication of application of registration of a geographical indication
Opposition to the registration of a geographical indication Matters related to opposition to the
articles.text:
registration, procedure for opposition to the
registration and appeal against the decision on
opposition to the registration of a geographical
indication are handled in the same way as
provided respectively.in Articles 194, 195 and
196 of this Law.
Section 4: Registration of a geographical
indication, its publication and invalidation

articles.heading: Registration and publication of registration of a geographical indication Matters related to the registration and
articles.text:
publication of registration of a geographical
272

articles.heading: Amendment of the registration of a geographical indication
Invalidation of the registration of a geographical indication An interested person may apply to the
articles.text:
competent court to invalidate the registration
of a geographical indication if he or she
indicates at least one of the following grounds:
(a) if a geographical indication does not
indicate the territory, region or locality
of the country in which the product
originates;
(b) if a geographical indication does not
indicate the quality and reputation of a
product or other characteristics that are
essentially attributable to its
geographical origin;
(c) if the quality, reputation or other
specific characteristic of the product
indicated on the geographical
indication cannot be attributed
essentially to its geographical origin;
(d) if a geographical indication is contrary
to public order or morality;
(e) if a geographical indication is not, or
has ceased to be, protected in its
273
country of origin;
(f) if a geographical indication misleads
and makes the public consider that the
products originate from a different
territory;
(g) if a geographical indication is identical
with the term customary in common
language in the Republic of Rwanda as
the common name for the relevant
product;
(h) a geographical indication is prejudicial
to a prior mark applied for or registered
in good faith, or acquired through use
in good faith in the Republic of
Rwanda.
Section 5: Rights conferred by registration
of a geographical indication

articles.heading: Right to use a geographical indication (1) The registration of a geographical indication confers on owners the
articles.text:
exclusive rights to its use on the
territory of the Republic of Rwanda.
274
(2) However, a registered geographical
indication cannot be subject to a
licence contract.

articles.heading: Civil proceedings against infringement of the right to use a geographical indication An interested person may initiate civil
articles.text:
proceedings before the competent court in
order to prevent or stop the following acts
related to a geographical indication:
(a) the use, in the designation or
presentation of the product, of any
means which indicates or suggests that
this product originates from another
geographical region in a manner which
misleads any person as to the
geographical origin of the product;
(b) any use of the geographical indication
which constitutes an act of unfair
competition;
(c) the use of a geographical indication
identifying wines for wines not
originating in the place indicated by the
geographical indication in question, or
identifying spirits for spirits not
originating in the place indicated by the
277

articles.heading: Refusal to register a mark identical with, or containing a geographical indication
Duration of protection of the registered geographical indication and its renewal (1) A registered geographical indication is
articles.text:
protected for a period of 10 years from
the filing date of the application for
registration.
(2) The duration of protection of a registered
geographical indication can be
indefinitely renewed for consecutive
periods of 10 years each, upon request of
the owner of a registered geographical
indication. The renewal of registration of
a geographical indication is subject to
payment of the prescribed fee.
(3) However, a grace period of six months is
granted for the payment of the fee for
renewal of the protection of the
registered geographical indication after
the deadline for payment. The payment
made during the grace period is subject

(4) If the fee for renewal of a geographical

278
CHAPTER VIII: COMMON
PROVISIONS TO INDUSTRIAL
PROPERTY

articles.heading: Person eligible to register an industrial property The person eligible to register an industrial
articles.text:
property is:
(a) a Rwandan who has his or her habitual
residence in the Republic of Rwanda or
legal entity which has its headquarters
in the Republic of Rwanda or a
company or an industry which has real
and effective industrial or business
establishments located in the Republic
of Rwanda;
(b) a national of a country party to Paris
Convention for the Protection of
Industrial Property or a national of a
country member of World Trade
Organisation regarding any application
before the competent authority and
enforcement of their rights in the
Republic of Rwanda;
279
(c) a national of a country not party to Paris
Convention for the Protection of
Industrial Property and a national of
country not a member of the World
Trade Organisation, who is domiciled
or who has real and effective industrial
or business establishments in the
territory of one of the countries parties
to Paris Convention or member of
World Trade Organisation regarding
any application before the competent
authority and enforcement of their
rights in the Republic of Rwanda;
(d) a person who is not referred to in
Subparagraphs (a), (b) and (c) of this
Article may apply for registration and
protection of his or her creation or
innovation taking into account the
interest for Rwanda or insofar as his or
her country of origin or in which he is
domiciled grants equivalent protection
to Rwandans.
280

articles.heading: Industrial property authorised agent (1) The applicant whose habitual residence or principal place of business is located
articles.text:
in the Republic of Rwanda may be
represented by an industrial property
agent authorised by the competent
authority.
(2) The applicant whose habitual residence
or principal place of business is located
outside the Republic of Rwanda is
represented by an industrial property
agent authorised by the competent
authority to carry out his or her
profession in the Republic of Rwanda.
(3) An applicant required to use, or
wishing to use an industrial property
authorised agent for any application,
notifies the competent authority in
writing of his or her nominated agent.
(4) An Order of the Minister determines
modalities for the use of an industrial
281
property agent and the format for the
power of attorney.

articles.heading: Provision of information and documents relating to foreign application with regard to industrial property
articles.text:
(1) The applicant claiming, in the Republic
of Rwanda, for the protection of
industrial property which is similar to
that for which he claimed in the
application filed abroad, indicates to
the competent authority the date and
number of the application he or she
filed abroad.
(2) The competent authority may request
the applicant to provide the following
documents:
(a) a copy of any communication
concerning the results of any search or
examination carried out in respect of
the foreign application;
(b) a certified copy of the certificate of
industrial property granted following
the foreign application;
282
(c) a copy of the final decision indicating
that the application was rejected
following a foreign application;
(d) a copy of the final decision invalidating
the industrial property certificate or
any other title of the industrial property
protection.

articles.heading: Rights to an industrial property
Notification for the receipt of the application for registration of an industrial property An application for registration of an industrial
articles.text:
property which fulfils the requirements give
the owner the right to be notified on receipt of
the application by the competent authority. The
notice states the following:
283
(a) date and hour on which the application
was filed;
(b) application number; and
(c) other necessary information
determined by the competent
authority.

articles.heading: Right of priority (1) An application for registration of industrial property may contain a claim
articles.text:
to a priority filing date in accordance
with the Paris Convention or any other
international convention to which the
Republic of Rwanda is party.
(2) A request of priority date may be filled
in respect of one or more previous
national, regional, or international
applications, filed by the applicant or
his or her rightful representative in a
State party to Paris Convention or the
World Trade Organisation.
(3) The priority date is 12 months from the
filing date of the first application for
A
284
which the right to priority is claimed.
However, this period is six months for
marks.

articles.heading: Requirements for making a request for a priority right (1) A request of priority date is accepted if
articles.text:
(a) it indicates the date and number of the
previous application and the State
where it has been filed;
(b) the applicant provides a copy of the
previous application, certified by the
authority with which this previous
application has been filed.
(2) When the copy of the previous application
is in a language which is not one of the
official languages in Rwanda, the applicant
provides a translated copy in one of the
official languages in Rwanda.
(3) If the application does not meet the
requirements provided in Sub paragraph
(b) of Paragraph (1) of this Article, the
competent authority requests the applicant
285
to fulfil the requirements within 30 days
from the date the applicant has been
notified.
(4) If the applicant does not fulfil the
requirements within the time limits
referred to in Paragraph (3) of this Article,
the request is not considered.

articles.heading: Effect of priority An application filled which include a request of priority date in the Republic of Rwanda in
articles.text:
accordance with Article 255 of this Law,
invalidates another similar application made in
the interval in the Republic of Rwanda, even if
acts including publication or use of the relevant
industrial property have been performed.

articles.heading: Withdrawal of an application for registration of an industrial property (1) An applicant for a registration of an
articles.text:
industrial property may withdraw the
application at any time during its
pendency by submitting a written
request to the competent authority.
286
(2) When the application has been
withdrawn, a subsequent application
can be filed in respect of the same
industrial property. If such subsequent
application is filed, it is regarded as the
first application in respect of that
industrial property.
(3) Priority rights are not granted based on
the withdrawn application.

articles.heading: Correction of errors (1) The competent authority requests the applicant in writing to correct any
articles.text:
clerical errors including those related
to translation, to mistakes appearing in
any application or document filed with
such authority as long as it does not
affect the application in substance.
(2) The applicant may, whenever
necessary, request in writing to the
competent authority the authorization
to correct clerical errors referred to in
Paragraph (1) of this Article.
287

articles.heading: Extension of time limits (1) The competent authority may, upon request by the interested person and on
articles.text:
reasonable grounds, extend the time
limits up to the same amount of time as
is provided for by this Law with regard
to correcting errors appearing in the
application file, completing the
application file, making an appeal
against a decision, to making an
opposition or cancellation of rights for
the non-use of industrial proprty.
(2) A request for the extension of time
limits is made in writing and is
accompanied with the statement of the
grounds for the extension before expiry
of the existing time limits and after
payment of a prescribed fee.

articles.heading: Keeping the industrial property registers (1) The competent authority keeps the following registers
Information update (1) The owner of a registered industrial property rights notifies to the competent
articles.text:
authority any change on the following:
(a) contact address of the owner of an
industrial property rights;
289
(b) industrial property authorised agent;
(c) other non-substantive administrative
information required.
(2) The competent authority updates the
information in the relevant register.
(3) Updating information is subject to
payment of a prescribed fee.

articles.heading: Reinstatement of rights (1) The owner of an industrial property who lost rights on such a property for
articles.text:
non-payment of maintenance fee
within the time limits provided for by
this Law may, on a reasonable ground,
request the competent authority to
reinstate his or her rights.
(2) The request for reinstatement of rights
is made in writing within a period of 12
months from the expiry date of the
deadline for the payment of
maintenance fee and after payment of a
prescribed fee.
290

articles.heading: First application principle If two or more persons have the same invention, utility model, industrial design,
articles.text:
layout-design of integrated circuit or mark but
independently of each other, the principle of
first applicant applies when it comes to
granting the priority date.

articles.heading: Owner of rights on an industrial property which was made during the execution of an employment contract
articles.text:
(1) If an invention, utility model, industrial
design, or the layout-design of
integrated circuit which are made by an
employee during the execution of an
employment contract, the right to apply
for the registration or certificate
belongs to the employer, unless
otherwise provided in the employment
contract.
(2) If an invention, utility model, industrial
design, or a layout-design of integrated
291
circuit has an economic value that is
higher than that which the both parties
could reasonably foresee at the time the
employment contract was concluded,
the employee is entitled to equitable
remuneration considering the value of
the invention, utility model, industrial
design, or the layout-design of
integrated circuit.

articles.heading: Owner of rights on an industrial property which was made out of the employment contract (1) An employee has the right to apply for a
articles.text:
registration certificate for an invention,
utility model, industrial design, or a
layout-design of integrated circuit if he or
she made them:
(a) without any obligation under his or
her employment contract;
292
(b) in his or her employer’s field of
activities;
(c) using the data, means or knowledge
available to him or her through his or
her employment.
(2) If the employer makes his or her interest
in such an invention, utility model,
industrial design, or a layout-design of
integrated circuit known to the employee,
he or she may request the grant of all or
part of the rights to the invention, utility
model, industrial design, or a layoutdesign of integrated circuit of the
employee in exchange for remuneration
to be agreed upon between the employee
and employer.
(3) If the employee and the employer cannot
reach an agreement, they refer the matter
to the competent court.
293

articles.heading: Use of industrial property title for security or guarantee An industrial property title may be used as
articles.text: security or guarantee.

articles.heading: Succession over the right to an industrial property An exclusive right to an invention, utility
articles.text:
model, industrial design, layout-design of
integrated circuit and to a mark may be subject
to succession.
CHAPTER IX: PROTECTION AGAINST
ACTS OF UNFAIR COMPETITION
Section One: General Principles

articles.heading: Protection against unfair competition A commercial, industrial or artistic activity emanating from the protected intellectual
articles.text:
294
property is protected against acts of unfair
competition.
Section 2: Acts of unfair competition

articles.heading: Acts of unfair competition For the purposes of the protection of intellectual property, the following acts
Causing confusion in another’s enterprise or activities (1) Any act or practice, in the course of
articles.text:
industrial or commercial activities, that
causes, or is likely to cause, confusion
with respect to a competitor’s or
another’s enterprise or his/her
activities, in particular, with regard to
the products or services offered by such
enterprise, constitutes an act of unfair
competition causing confusion.
(2) Confusion may be caused with respect
to:
(a) a registered or non-registered mark;
(b) a trade name;
(c) a business identifier other than a
mark or trade name;
(d) the appearance of a product;
(e) the presentation of products or
services;
296
(f) a celebrity or a well-known
fictional character.

articles.heading: Discrediting another’s enterprise or its activities (1) Any false or unjustified allegation, in
articles.text:
the course of industrial or commercial
activities, that discredits, or is likely to
discredit, a competitor’s or another
person’s enterprise or activities, in
particular, the products or services
offered by such enterprise, constitutes
an act of unfair competition
discrediting another’s enterprise or its
activities.
(2) Discrediting may arise out of
commercial advertising or promotion
and may occur with respect to:
(a) the manufacturing process of the
product;
(b) the suitability of a product or service
for a particular purpose;
297
(c) the quality or quantity or other
characteristics of the product;
(d) the conditions on which products or
services are offered or provided;
(e) the price of products or services or
the manner in which it is calculated.

articles.heading: Misleading the public (1) Any indication or words in the course of industrial or commercial activities
articles.text:
that mislead, or are likely to mislead
the public with respect to an enterprise
or its activities, in particular, the
products or services offered by such
enterprise, constitute acts of unfair
competition misleading the public.
(2) A misleading act may arise out of
commercial advertising or promotion
and may occur with respect to the
following:
(a) the manufacturing process of the
product;
298
(b) the suitability of a product or
service for a particular purpose;
(c) the quality or quantity or other
characteristics of the product;
(d) the nature of the product, designs,
marks and the patent of a
competitor or an enterprise whose
activities are similar to those of
another enterprise;
(e) the geographical origin of the
product or services;
(f) the conditions on which products or
services are offered or provided;
(g) the price of products or services or
the manner in which it is calculated.

articles.heading: Damaging another’s goodwill or reputation (1) Any act or practice, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, that
articles.text:
damages, or is likely to damage, the
(
299
goodwill or reputation of a
competitor’s or another’s enterprise
constitute an act of unfair competition,
regardless of whether such act or
practice causes confusion.
(2) Damaging another’s goodwill or
reputation may, in particular, result
from the dilution of the goodwill or
reputation attached to:
(a) a mark, whether registered or not,
protected by its celebrity;
(b) a trade name;
(c) a business identifier other than a
mark or a trade name;
(d) the appearance of a product;
(e) the presentation of a product or
service;
(f) a celebrity or a well-known fictional
character.
(
300
(3) For the purposes of provisions of this
article “dilution of goodwill or
reputation” means the lessening of the
distinctive character or advertising
value of a mark, trade name or other
business identifier, the appearance of a
product or the presentation of a product
or service or of a celebrity or wellknown fictional character.
