articles.heading: Unauthorised use of technical know-how Any unauthorized use of a patented invention, utility model, industrial design or a layoutdesign, mark, technical formul
articles.text:
combinations or manufacturing method of a
competitor or other company constitutes an act
of unfair competition.

articles.heading: Unfair competition in respect of secret information (1) Any act or practice, in the course of
articles.text:
industrial or commercial activities, that
(
301
result in the disclosure, acquisition or use
by others of secret information without
the consent of the person lawfully in
control of the rightful holder and in a
manner contrary to honest commercial
practices shall constitute an act of unfair
competition.
(2) Disclosure, acquisition or use of secret
information by others without the
consent of the rightful holder may, in
particular, result from:
(a) industrial and commercial espionage;
(b) breach of contract;
(c) breach of confidence;
(d) inducement to commit any of the acts
referred to in Subparagraphs (a) to (c)
of this Paragraph;
(e) acquisition of secret information by a
third party who knew that one of the
acts referred to in subparagraphs (a)
to (d) of this paragraph was initiated
during the process of acquisition of
such an information or indicated its
lack of awareness.
302
(3) For the purposes of this Article,
information is considered secret under
the following reasons:
(a) if it is unknown or not easily
accessible due to its nature or the
way it is kept;
(b) if it has commercial value because
it is secret;
(c) if the holder has taken reasonable
steps to keep it secret.

articles.heading: Civil proceedings against unfair competition An intellectual property owner harmed, or likely to be harmed by an act of unfair
articles.text:
competition, has the right to initiate civil
proceedings before the competent court, or to
request for the cessation of such an act where,
through an act contrary to honest industrial and
commercial use, a manufacturer, trader,
producer or craftsman damages his or her
credibility, takes away his or her customers or
harms his or her capacity for competition.
303
TITLE III: COPYRIGHTS AND
RELATED RIGHTS
CHAPTER ONE: SCOPE OF
COPYRIGHTS AND RELATED RIGHTS

articles.heading: Components of copyrights and related rights The components of copyrights and related rights are the following
Protected works The protected original literary, artistic or scientific works include the following
Derivative works and collections of works protected (1) Protected derivative works include translations, adaptations, arrangements
articles.text:
and other transformations of works.
306
(2) Protected collections of works include
works of expression of folklore or of
simple facts or mere data such as
encyclopaedia, anthologies, collections
of data, whether in machine readable
form or other form, provided that such
collections are original intellectual
creations by reason of the selection or
arrangement of their contents.
(3) The protection of derivative works or
collections of works do not affect the
protection of existing works used in the
making of such works.

articles.heading: Protected work on the basis of territoriality The protection of a literary, artistic or scientific
articles.text:
work on the basis of territoriality applies to the
following:
307
(a) work of an author or any other entitled
person who is a national of the Republic
of Rwanda, or has his or her habitual
residence or headquarters in the Republic
of Rwanda;
(b) audio-visual work, the producer of which
is a national of the Republic of Rwanda or
has his or her habitual residence or
headquarters in the Republic of Rwanda;
(c) work first published in the Republic of
Rwanda;
(d) work of architecture erected on the
territory of the Republic Rwanda and
other artistic work incorporated in a
building located on the territory the
Republic of Rwanda;
(e) work that is eligible for protection in
accordance with the Berne Convention for
the Protection of Literary and Artistic
Works, or any other international
convention to which Rwanda is party;
(f) if the country of origin of the author or in
which he or she is resident grants
equivalent protection to works from the
Republic of Rwanda.
308

articles.heading: Works excluded from protection The protection of works does not extend to
articles.text:
(a) official texts of a legislative,
administrative and judicial nature, and
official translations of such texts;
(b) news of the day or miscellaneous facts
having the character of mere items of
press information;
(c) any idea, procedure, system, method of
operation, concept, principle,
discovery or mere data, regardless of
the form in which it is described,
explained, illustrated, or embodied in
such work.

articles.heading: Requirements for protection of a work (1) A work is protected when it is original
articles.text:
(2) An original work is protected whether
registered or not.
309
(3) The protection of an original work
starts from the beginning of its
creation, even if it is not incorporated
to a medium.
(4) An original work is deemed to have
been created by the sole fact of its
creation, irrespective of any public
disclosure, even if it is incomplete and
during the time it is designed by its
author.
(5) Protection of a work is independent of
the mode, form of expression, utility,
quality and purpose of the work.

articles.heading: Originality of a work A work is original if it originates from the author, is not a copy of another work, and is the
articles.text:
product of the author’s exercise of skill, effort
and judgment.

articles.heading: Presumption of ownership of copyright (1) An author of a work is presumed to be the copyright owner
articles.text:
(2) An author of an unregistered work is
presumed as the owner of the copyright if
310
it is sufficient for his or her name to be
indicated on the work.
(3) The provisions of Paragraph (2) of this
Article are applicable even if the name is
a pseudonym, where the pseudonym
leaves no doubt as to the identity of the
author.
(4) In the case of an anonymous work or
pseudonymous work that leaves doubt,
the publisher whose name appears on the
work is, in the absence of proof to the
contrary, deemed to represent the author,
and in this capacity, he or she is entitled
to protect and enforce the author’s rights.
(5) The provisions of Paragraph (4) of this
Article do not apply when the author
reveals his identity and establishes his or
her claim to authorship of the work.

articles.heading: Filing of an application for registration of a work (1) An application for registration of a work
articles.text:
is filed by filling in a form provided for
311
this purpose, which is prescribed by the
competent authority.
(2) Filing of the application is subject to
payment of a prescribed fee.

articles.heading: Setting the filing date of application for registration of a work The competent authority sets as the filing date
articles.text:
of application for registration of a work, the
date of receipt of the application, and records
the work and related right in the register of
copyrights.
Section 2: Protected rights
Subsection one: Moral rights

articles.heading: Moral rights of an author (1) An author of a work enjoys the following moral rights
articles.text:
(a) claim the authorship, in particular
to have his or her name indicated on
the work or a copy of the work and
in connection with any public use
312
of his or her work, as far as
practicable;
(b) object to any distortion, mutilation
or other modification of, or other
derogatory action in relation to his
or her work if prejudicial to his or
her honour or reputation;
(c) not have his or her name known or
use a pseudonym.
(2) Moral rights of an author cannot be
assigned or licenced.
Subsection 2: Economic rights

articles.heading: Economic rights of an author (1) An author of a work has the exclusive right to do or to authorise the following
articles.text:
acts:
(a) to reproduce his or her work;
(b) to translate his or her work;
313
(c) to adapt, arrange or transform his or her
work;
(d) to rent or lend, or to authorise the
renting or lending to the public the
original or a copy of an audio-visual
work, a work embodied in a
phonogram, or a computer program,
except if such renting or lending for
educational or non-profit purposes for
the benefit of the general public;
(e) to distribute or authorise distribution to
the public of the original or a copy of
his or her work for sale;
(f) to transfer ownership of a work;
(g) to communicate his or her work to the
public by any means, including by
broadcast or public performance.
(2) The right of distribution does not apply
to the original or a copy of the work
314
that has been put on the market or been
subject to a sale or other transfer of
ownership authorised by the owner of
the copyright.
(3) In case of original graphic and threedimensional works of art or original
manuscript, the author or his or her
heirs have the inalienable right to have
a share of the resale price of the work
subsequent to the first transfer of
ownership of the work by the author.
(4) The competent authority determines
the amount of the share of the resale
price of the work.

articles.heading: Economic rights of work derived from folklore (1) The following acts are subject to payment
articles.text:
of royalties:
(a) the use of work derived from national
folklore for profit making purposes;
315
(b) a transfer of ownership in whole or in
part, for profit making purposes, of
work derived from the folklore or any
exclusive licence granted on such
work, for profit making purposes.
(2) The competent authority determines the
royalties for the use or transfer of rights on
the work derived from the folklore for
profit making purposes, and modalities for
payment.
(3) Twenty-five per cent of any royalties paid
is reserved to fund activities aimed at
creative works promotion.
Subsection 3: Limitations to economic
rights on a work

articles.heading: Private reproduction of a work for personal purposes (1) The private reproduction of a published
articles.text:
work by a natural person in a single copy is
permitted without the authorisation of the
316
author and without the obligation of
payment of royalties.
(2) However, the provisions of Paragraph (1)
of this Article does not extend to the
reproduction of:
(a) a work of architecture in the form of
building or similar construction;
(b) the form of reprography of the whole or
of a substantial part of a book or of a
musical work in the form of notation;
(c) the whole or of a substantial part of a
database in digital form;
(d) a computer program.

articles.heading: Permitted temporary reproduction of a work Temporary reproduction of a work is permitted if
articles.text:
(a) it is done in the process of a digital
transmission of the work or an act of
317
making a digitally stored work
perceptible;
(b) it is done by an authorised a natural
person or entity entitled to make that
transmission or to make the work
perceptible;
(c) it is incidental to the transmission, that
occurs during the normal operation of
the equipment used and entails the
automatic deletion of the copy without
enabling the electronic retrieval of the
work for any other purpose than those
referred to in Subparagraphs (a) and (b)
of this Article.

articles.heading: Free use of a published work in the form of quotation (1) The use, in the form of quotation or of a
articles.text:
short part of a published work is
permitted without authorisation of the
author and without payment of royalties,
provided that the use is compatible with
fair practice and does not exceed the
extent justified by the purpose.
318
(2) A quotation or short part of a work is
accompanied by an indication of source
and the name of the author, if his or her
name appears in the work from which the
quotation is taken.

articles.heading: Use of a work for teaching purposes (1) For teaching purposes, the following acts are permitted in respect of a work without
articles.text:
the authorisation of the author and without
payment of royalties:
(a) the use of a work for teaching purposes
by way of illustration, broadcasting,
sound or visual recordings;
(b) the reproduction by reprographic
means, for teaching or for the holding
of examinations at educational nonprofit making institutions, to the extent
justified by the purpose;
(c) various articles lawfully published in
magazines or gazettes, brief extracts of
a work published lawfully or a short
creative work lawfully published.
319
(2) However, the acts referred to in Paragraph
(1) of this Article are subject to the
obligation to indicate the source and the
name of the author if the name appears on
a work.

articles.heading: Reprographic reproduction of a work by libraries or archive services Libraries or archive services whose activities
articles.text:
are not directly or indirectly profit-making
may, without the consent of the author or other
holder of copyright, make a necessary number
of copies of a work by means of reprographic
reproduction, where:
(a) the work reproduced is a published
article, other short work or short extract
of a work;
(b) the purpose of the reproduction is to
satisfy the request of a natural person;
(c) the library or archive service is satisfied
that the copy will be used solely for the
320
purposes of study, scholarship or private
research;
(d) the act of reproduction is an isolated case
occurring, if repeated, on separate and
unrelated occasions, and there is no
collective licence available;
(e) the copy is made in order to preserve or
replace a copy which has been lost,
destroyed or rendered unusable or which
is in the permanent collection of another
library or archive service.

articles.heading: Free use of a work for judicial or administrative purposes The use of a work for judicial or administrative
articles.text:
procedure purposes is permitted without the
consent of the author and without payment of
royalties, on the condition that the extent of
such use does not exceed that justified by the
intended purpose.
321

articles.heading: Free use of a work for informational purposes (1) The following acts in respect of information on a work are permitted
articles.text:
without the consent of the author and
without payment of royalties:
(a) the reproduction by the press, the
broadcasting or the communication to
the public, of an article published in
newspapers or periodicals on current
economic, political, social or religious
topics, or of a broadcast work of the
same character, where the right to
reproduction, broadcasting or
communication to the public is not
expressly reserved;
(b) the reproduction or communication to
the public, for the purpose of reporting
short current events by means of
photography, cinematography, or
through broadcasting or communication
by wire, of a work seen or heard during
such event, to the extent justified by the
intended informatory purpose;
(c) the reproduction in the press, the
322
broadcasting or other communication to
the public of political speeches, lectures,
addresses, sermons or other works of the
same nature delivered in public, or
speeches delivered during legal
proceedings, to the extent justified by
the purpose of providing current
information the authors remaining with
the right to publish the collection of
those works.
(2) However, the acts referred to in Paragraph
(1) of this Article indicate the source and
the name of the author as far as practicable.

articles.heading: Free use of images or photographs of works that are located in a place open to the public (1) The following acts related to images,
articles.text:
photographic works, works of applied
art, an image of a work of architecture
that are permanently located in a place
open to the public are permitted
without the consent of the author and
without payment of royalties:
(a) reproduction;
(b) broadcast;
(c) communication to the public by
wire.
323
(2) However, if the image of the work is
the main subject of such reproduction,
broadcast or communication and if it is
used for commercial purposes, consent
and payment of a royalties are required.

articles.heading: Free reproduction and adaptation of computer programs (1) The legitimate owner of a copy of a
articles.text:
computer program may, without the
author’s authorization or payment of
royalty, make a copy or adapt this program,
provided that the copy or adaptation is
required for:
(a) use of the computer program for
purposes for which the program has
been obtained;
(b) archiving purposes and in order to
replace the copy lawfully held where
that copy was lost, damaged or made
unusable.
324
(2) A copy or adaptation of a program made
under Paragraph (1) of this Article is
destroyed where the contract for extended
possession of the copy of the computer
program ceases to be lawful. The
destruction of such a program is made
within six months after the expiry of the
contract.

articles.heading: Free ephemeral recording by a broadcasting organisation (1) A broadcasting organisation may, without
articles.text:
the consent of the author and without
payment of royalty, make an ephemeral
recording by means of its own facilities
and for the purposes of its own broadcasts
of a work it is authorized to broadcast.
(2) A broadcasting organisation is required to
destroy such a recording within six months
of it having been made, unless a different
agreement has been made.

articles.heading: Free public performance of a work Public performance of a work is permitted without the consent of the author and without
articles.text:
325
payment of royalties if it is done:
(a) during an official or religious ceremonies,
where the public performance is not for
profit;
(b) as part of the educational or public
awareness activities of the government or
non-profit making organisation, where the
public performance of a work is not for
profit;
(c) or as part of the teaching activities of an
educational institution, where the work is
performed to staff, students or organisation
of students or other persons directly
involved in activities of the institution.

articles.heading: Free importation of a work for personal purposes The importation of a lawfully obtained copy of
articles.text:
a work by a person for his or her own personal
purposes is permitted without the consent of
the author and without payment of royalties.
326

articles.heading: Free reproduction of a work for persons who are blind, visually impaired, or print disabled
articles.text:
(1) An authorized entity can, without the
consent of the author or copyright
holder and without payment of
royalties, make an accessible format
copy of a work, obtain from another
authorised entity an accessible format
copy, and supply those copies to
persons who are blind, visually
impaired, or print disabled by any
means, including by non-commercial
lending or by electronic
communication by wire or wireless
means, and undertake any intermediate
steps to achieve those objectives, when
the following conditions are met:
(a) the authorised entity wishing to
undertake said activity has lawful
access to that work or a copy of that
work;
(b) the work is converted to an accessible
format copy, which may include any
327
means needed to navigate information
in the accessible format, but does not
introduce changes other than those
needed to make the work accessible to
the person who is blind, visually
impaired, or print disabled;
(c) such accessible format copies are
supplied exclusively to be used by
persons who are blind, visually
impaired, or print disabled;
(d) the activity is undertaken on a nonprofit basis.
(2) A person who is blind, visually
impaired or print disabled, or someone
acting on his or her behalf may, without
the consent and without payment of
royalties, make an accessible format
copy of a work for the personal use of
the beneficiary person or otherwise
may assist the beneficiary person to
make and use accessible format copies
where the beneficiary person has
328
lawful access to that work or a copy of
that work.
(3) Provisions of this Article apply to the
works that are in the form of text,
notation or related illustrations,
whether published or otherwise made
publicly available in any media,
including works in audio form, such as
audiobooks. They also apply to objects
of related rights as necessary to make
accessible format copies.

articles.heading: Free distribution or importation of an accessible format copy for persons who are blind, visually impaired, or
articles.text:
print disabled
(1) An authorised entity can, without the
authorisation of the author or copyright
holder and without payment of
royalties, distribute or make available
accessible format copies if:
329
(a) such copies are for the exclusive use
of persons who are blind, visually
impaired, or print disabled;
(b) it is intended to make available such
copies directly to a person who is
blind, visually impaired, or print
disabled from another country party
to the Marrakesh Treaty;
(c) the permission granted applies
provided that prior to the
distribution or making available the
originating authorised entity did not
know or did not have reasonable
grounds to know that the accessible
format copy would be used for other
than persons who are blind, visually
impaired, or print disabled.
(2) Such distribution or making available
accessible format copies is limited to:
(a) certain special cases;
330
(b) matters that do not conflict with a
normal exploitation of the work or
object of related rights;
(c) matters that do not unreasonably
prejudice the legitimate interests of
the copyright holder.
(3) A person who is blind, visually
impaired, or print disabled, or someone
acting on his or her behalf, or an
authorised entity, is permitted to import
an accessible format copy for the
benefit of that disabled person, without
the without the authorisation of the
author or copyright holder and without
payment of royalties.
(4) Provisions of this Article apply to the
works that are in the form of text,
notation or related illustrations,
whether published or otherwise made
publicly available in any media,
including works in audio form, such as
audiobooks. They also apply to objects
of related rights as necessary to make
accessible format copies.
331

articles.heading: Obligations on the use of a work without authorisation The free use of a work without the authorisation of the right holder referred to in
articles.text:
Articles 291, 292, 293, 294, 295, 296, 297,
298, 299, 300, 301, 302, 303 and 304 of this
Law does not prejudice the normal use of a
work, related rights or legitimate interests of
the right holder.
Subsection 4: Duration of protection of
copyrights

articles.heading: Duration of protection of moral rights in a work Moral rights in a work have no limitation in
articles.text:
time, are imprescriptible, are not transferrable
when the author is still alive or deceased.

articles.heading: Duration of protection of economic rights in a work Economic rights in a work are protected during
articles.text:
the life of the author and for 50 years after his
332
or her death. The period of protection of
economic rights in a work extends to the end
of the calendar year in which the property
rights expire.

articles.heading: Duration of protection of economic rights in a work of joint authorship Economic rights in a work of joint authorship
articles.text:
are protected during the life of the last
surviving author and for 50 years after his or
her death.

articles.heading: Duration of protection of economic rights in an anonymous work or a pseudonymous work (1) Economic rights in a work published
articles.text:
anonymously or under a pseudonym
are protected in one of the following
periods:
(a) for a period of 50 years from the
date of the making of the work;
333
(b) for a period 50 years from the date
on which such a work was
published for the first time;
(c) for a period of 50 years from the
date on which such a work was
made accessible to the public.
(2) However, where, before the expiration
of the periods referred to in Paragraph
(1) of this Article, the author’s identity
is revealed or is no longer in doubt,
articles 307 and 308 apply.

articles.heading: Duration of protection of economic rights in a collective work or a posthumous work Economic rights in a collective work or a
articles.text:
posthumous work are protected in one of the
following periods:
(a) for a period of 50 years from the date
of the making of the work;
(b) for a period 50 years from the date on
which such a work was published for
the first time;
334
(c) for a period of 50 years from the date
on which such a work was made
accessible to the public.

articles.heading: Duration of protection of economic rights in a work of applied art Economic rights in a work of applied art are
articles.text:
protected for a period of 25 years from the date
of the making of the work.

articles.heading: Period in which a work passes into the public domain (1) A work passes into the public domain if
articles.text:
(a) the term of its protection expires;
(b) the owner of copyright has waived his
or her right on such a work.
(2) The waiver of rights referred to in
Subparagraph (b) of Paragraph (1) of this
Article is done in a written statement
communicated to the public through any
means and after examining if such a waiver
does not prejudice prior contracts relating
to such a work.
335
(3) Any person can use a work that has passed
into the public domain without complying
with the provisions of Article 289 of this
Law.
Subsection 5: Owner of economic rights in a
work

articles.heading: Ownership of a work of joint authorship (1) The co-authors of a work are the original owners of the moral and
articles.text:
economic rights in such a work.
(2) If a work of joint authorship cannot be
used separately, the co-authors are the
owners jointly but each of them may
assign his or her share in the work and
may undertake separate proceedings
for infringement of copyrights.
(3) If a work of joint authorship consists of
parts that can be used separately and
can be reproduced, performed or
executed in a different manner, the
336
author of each part is entitled to the
rights on the part that corresponds to
his or her personal contribution to that
work, but the co-authors remain the coowners of the whole work.

articles.heading: Ownership of a collective work The owner of moral and economic rights in a collective work is the person who initiated its
articles.text:
creation and under whose responsibility the
work was created.

articles.heading: Ownership of a work created under an employment contract (1) If a work is created by an author
articles.text:
employed by a person in the execution
of a work contract, the owner of the
moral rights is the employed author,
unless provided otherwise in the
contract of employment.
(2) The economic rights are considered
assigned to the employer or his or her
representative if the work was created
in execution of an employment
contract which aims at carrying out
creative activity.
337
(3) However, the employee is the owner of
economic rights on a work that he or
she created without it being stipulated
in the contract of employment.
(4) A work created by a Rwanda’s civil
servant in the execution of contract of
employment is owned by the Republic
of Rwanda unless provided otherwise
in the contract of employment.

articles.heading: Ownership of a work created under commission If the creation of a work is commissioned by a
articles.text:
person in exchange for remuneration, the
economic rights to that work belong to the
person who commissioned the work, unless
otherwise stipulated in a written contract
governing such a commission.

articles.heading: Ownership of audio-visual work (1) A producer of an audio-visual work is the owner of the economic rights,
articles.text:
unless provided otherwise in a contract.
338
(2) However, co-authors of the audiovisual work and other authors of the
pre-existing works included in or
adapted for the making of the audiovisual work, maintain their economic
rights in their contributions or preexisting works, respectively, to the
extent that those contributions or preexisting work, can be subject of acts
covered by their economic rights
separately from the audio-visual work.

articles.heading: Ownership of economic rights on a photographic work (1) A creator of a photographic work is the
articles.text:
owner of the economic rights on such a
work.
(2) However, another person may be the owner
of the economic rights on such a work,
upon payment of a remuneration, by means
of a written contract, unless provided
otherwise in a contract.
339
Subsection 6: Assignment of economic
rights on a work

articles.heading: Assignment of economic rights on a work (1) Economic rights on a work are an exclusive property which may be
articles.text:
assigned in whole or in part.
(2) The owner of economic rights may
assign such rights to any person
through the work assignment contract
or through succession.

articles.heading: Assignment contract of economic rights on a work (1) An assignment contract for economic rights on a work indicates at least the
articles.text:
following:
(a) specific rights being assigned;
(b) duration of the assignment;
(c) territorial scope of the assignment,
or otherwise the assignment is
340
presumed to be limited to the
jurisdiction under which the
assignment contract was
concluded;
(d) amount of remuneration and mode
of payment.
(2) The assignment contract is valid if it is
made in writing and signed by both
parties.
(3) Economic rights which are not
explicitly mentioned in the contract are
presumed to be reserved for the author.

articles.heading: Transfer of an original work or its copies (1) If the author gives as a gift the original or a copy of his or her work to another
articles.text:
person, he or she is neither considered
to have assigned any of his or her
economic rights nor authorised to
perform any act concerning his or her
economic rights, unless the transfer
contract provides otherwise.
341
(2) Subject to provisions of Paragraph (1)
of this Article, the legitimate holder of
an original or a copy of the work enjoys
the right of presentation of the original
or copy to the public, unless the
transfer contract provides otherwise.
(3) The right referred to in Paragraph (2) of
this Article is not extended to persons
who are in possession of original or
copies of a work by means of renting or
any other means without having
acquired ownership of the economic
rights over the work.
Subsection 7: Licence of economic rights on
a work

articles.heading: Contractual licence for economic rights An author of a work may grant, by written contractual licence agreement signed by both
articles.text:
parties, an exclusive, semi-exclusive or nonexclusive licence to another person authorising
that person to engage in any act exercising an
economic right in relation to the work.
342

articles.heading: Content of the licence contract for economic rights on a work (1) A licence contract for economic rights
articles.text:
of a work indicates at least the
following:
(a) specific rights on the licence being
assigned;
(b) duration of the licence;
(c) territorial scope of the licence,
otherwise the licence is presumed to be
limited to the jurisdiction under which
the licence contract was concluded;
(d) amount of remuneration and mode of
payment.
(2) Economic rights which are not
mentioned in the contract are presumed
to be explicitly reserved to the author.

articles.heading: Licence for the use of an orphan work (1) A person who wants to use an orphan work applies for a licence to the
articles.text:
343
competent authority if he or she made
reasonable efforts to locate the owner
of the orphan work but failed to locate
him or her.
(2) If the competent authority is satisfied
that the applicant has made reasonable
efforts to locate the owner of the
orphan work and that the owner cannot
be located, the competent authority
may issue to the applicant a licence.
(3) A licence issued for the use of an
orphan wok is non-exclusive and is
subject to terms and conditions
determined by the competent authority.

articles.heading: Duration of collection of royalties over a licence for the use of an orphan work The owner of the work may, not later than five
articles.text:
years after the expiration of a licence issued in
respect of the orphan work, collect the
royalties fixed in the licence or, in default of
their payment, file an action to recover them in
the competent court.
Subsection 8: Publishing contract
344

articles.heading: Conditions of publishing contract (1) A copyright owner may assign, through a publishing contract, to a
articles.text:
publisher the right to make or to
authorise the making of a number of
graphic, mechanical, digital or copies
of the work, and to publish or
distribute them. While executing the
publishing contract, a publisher:
(a) does not, without the agreement of
the author, make any modification to
his or her work;
(b) indicates on each of the copies the
name of the author or his or her
pseudonym;
(c) determines:
(i) form and means of publication;
(ii) duration of the publishing contract;
(iii) number of copies of this
publication and how many copies
345
unsold after the expiration of the
contract are to be dealt with;
(iv)amount of remuneration and mode
of payment for the author in
accordance with the use and
revenue extracted from the use of
his or her work;
(v) manner of termination of the
publishing contract.
(2) Unless otherwise provided for in the
contract, new publication of the work
is not done without another
authorisation of author.

articles.heading: Limitation of economic rights of the publisher (1) The publisher is not permitted to transfer to third party, either by gift,
articles.text:
sale or by means of having company’s
shares, the profit extracted from
publishing contract, without previous
author’s authorization.
(2) In case of transfer of publishing
business in relation with the work and
when this transfer is likely to cause
346
injury to the author's economic or
moral interests, the author shall be
entitled to equitable compensation and
in case of failure of such compensation
the contract shall terminate, according
to the importance of the infringement.
(3) Where publishing business is exploited
by a legal entity, the acquisition of this
business by a natural person, associated
or not arising from liquidation of
business or sharing business assets
shall not be considered as assignment
of rights and shall require the author's
approval.

articles.heading: Duration of publishing contract (1) In case of a publishing contract with a determined duration, the publisher’s
articles.text:
rights immediately expire with the
determined period.
(2) However, in a period of three years after
the expiration of the determined period,
the publisher may sell the copies
remaining in the stock, except if during
that period the author prefers to take the
remaining copies and to pay the publisher
347
a remuneration equivalent to the value of
these copies.

articles.heading: Termination of the publishing contract (1) The publishing contract may be terminated when the publisher does not comply with
articles.text:
the terms of the contract or when the author
does not fulfil his or her duties.
(2) The publishing edition is considered to be
exhausted where two successive
purchasing orders for delivery of copies
have not been satisfied within six months
without any valid reason.
(3) Where publishing edition is exhausted, the
author may terminate the contract. In case
of author’s death during the publishing
edition, the contract is terminated with
regard to the part of the contract not
executed, except otherwise stipulated by a
new contract between the publisher and the
heirs of the author.
Subsection 9: Compulsory licence
348

articles.heading: Compulsory licence for a translation of a work (1) An interested person may apply to the Minister for a translation compulsory
articles.text:
licence in respect of the work, for teaching
or research purposes, if, in respect of a
work published in printed or an analogous
form of reproduction:
(a) if in a period of three years after the
date of the first publication of the work
in one of the official languages, the
work has not been published in another
official language; or
(b) the work has been translated into all of
the official languages but one or more
of the published translations are out of
print.
(2) A translation compulsory licence is nonexclusive and non-transferable, for the
domestic market, and permits the licenceholder, without authorisation of the
copyright owner, to translate the work into
the relevant languages and publish the
translation in printed or analogous forms of
reproduction.
349

articles.heading: Requirements for granting a translation compulsory licence (1) A translation compulsory licence may be
articles.text:
granted if the applicant proves that:
(a) he or she requested from the copyright
owner, the authorisation to translate the
work into other languages and was
denied such authorization on
commercial grounds;
(b) he or she made reasonable efforts to
contact the copyright owner but was
unable to find him or her.
(2) In case a translation compulsory licence
is granted, the person who is granted such
a licence must indicate the name of the
author and the original title of the work
on all copies of the translation made
under a translation compulsory licence.
(3) When granting the licence, the Minister
takes appropriate measures to ensure a
350
correct translation of the work and just
remuneration for the copyright owner
that is consistent with standards of
royalties for licences freely negotiated in
respect of the type of work that is the
subject of the translation compulsory
licence.
(4) However, a translation compulsory
licence is not granted if the author has
withdrawn from circulation all copies of
his or her work.

articles.heading: Expiry of a translation licence (1) The translation compulsory licence expires if
articles.text:
(a) a translation of that work is published
in official languages by the copyright
owner; or
(b) the translation of the work is done with
the authorisation of the copyright
owner at a reasonable remuneration in
respect of standards of the
determination of royalties.
351
(2) However, copies already made before the
translation compulsory licence expires
continue to be distributed until the stock is
exhausted.

articles.heading: Requirements for granting a reproduction compulsory licence (1) An interested person may apply to the
articles.text:
Minister for a reproduction compulsory
licence in respect of a work, for the
purpose of public interest, teaching or
research in respect a work published in
printed or an analogous form of
reproduction in the Republic of
Rwanda.
(2) A reproduction compulsory licence is
non-exclusive and non-transferable for
a domestic market.

articles.heading: Period for granting a reproduction compulsory licence (1) A compulsory licence for reproduction
articles.text:
of a work may be granted for the
following periods:
352
(a) three years from the date of first
publication of the edition for works of
the natural and physical sciences and
those of technology;
(b) seven years from the date of first
publication of the edition for works of
fiction, poetry, drama and music, and
for art books;
(c) five years from the date of first
publication of the edition for all other
works.
(2) If after expiry of a period referred to in
Paragraph (1) of this Article, there exist
copies of the work that have not been
distributed by the copyright owner for
reproduction or with his or her
authorisation at a reasonable price
given comparable works, or no
authorised copies of that work have
been on sale for a period of six months
at a reasonable price given to
comparable works, any interested
person may obtain a licence to
reproduce and publish such edition at a
reasonable price.
353

articles.heading: Requirements for granting a reproduction compulsory licence (1) A reproduction compulsory licence may
articles.text:
be granted if the applicant establishes that:
(a) he or she requested from the owner, the
authorisation to reproduce the work
and was denied the same on
commercial grounds;
(b) he or she made reasonable efforts to
contact the copyright owner to request
a licence but was unable to find him or
her.
(2) In case a reproduction compulsory licence
is granted, the person who is granted such
a licence must indicate the name of the
author and the original title of the work all
copies of the work reproduced under a
reproduction compulsory licence.
(3) When granting the compulsory licence, the
Minister takes appropriate measures to
ensure a faithful reproduction of the work
and just remuneration for the copyrights
owner that is consistent with standards of
royalties for licences freely negotiated in
354
respect of the type of work that is the
subject of the reproduction compulsory
licence.
(4) However, a reproduction compulsory
licence is not granted if the author has
withdrawn from circulation all copies of
his or her work.

articles.heading: Expiration of a reproduction compulsory licence (1) The reproduction compulsory licence expires if
articles.text:
(a) the reproduction of that work and
circulation were made by the copyright
owner;
(b) the reproduction was authorised by the
copyright owner on a reasonable price.
(2) However, copies already made before the
reproduction licence expires may continue
to be distributed until the stock is
exhausted.
CHAPTER II: CONTENT, SCOPE AND
DURATION OF RELATED RIGHTS
355
Section One: Protection of performance,
phonograms and broadcasts

articles.heading: Protection of performance A performance is protected if
articles.text:
(a) the performer is a national of the
Republic of Rwanda;
(b) it takes place on the territory of the
Republic of Rwanda;
(c) it is incorporated in a phonogram that
is protected;
(d) it has not been fixed in a phonogram
but is included in a broadcast
qualifying for protection;
(e) the performer is an audio-visual
performer who is not a national of the
Republic of Rwanda but has his or her
habitual residence in the Republic of
Rwanda.
356

articles.heading: Phonogram protected A phonogram is protected if at least the following is fulfilled
articles.text:
(a) the producer is a national of the
Republic of Rwanda;
(b) the first fixation of sounds on the
phonogram took place in the Republic
of Rwanda;
(c) the first publication of the phonogram
took place in the Republic of Rwanda.

articles.heading: Broadcast protected The broadcast is protected if
articles.text:
(a) the headquarter of the broadcasting
organisation is located in the Republic
of Rwanda;
(b) the broadcast is transmitted from
transmitters situated in the Republic of
Rwanda.
357

articles.heading: Duration for protection of a performance (1) The rights granted to performances are protected within a period of 50 years from
articles.text:
(a) the first month of the year that follows
the year of sounds and images fixation
if the performance has been fixed on a
phonogram;
(b) the first month of the year that follows
the year of the music execution or of
the performance if the music or the
performance has not been fixed on a
phonogram.
(2) The protection of performances does not
limit or cause prejudice to the protection of
copyrights for the work subjected to
performance.

articles.heading: Duration for protection of a phonogram (1) A phonogram is protected for a period of 50 years from
articles.text:
358
(a) the first month of the year that follows
the year of publication of the
phonogram;
(b) the first month of the year that follows
the year of the work fixation on the
phonogram;
(c) the first month of the year that follows
the year of the sound recording if the
phonogram has not been published.
(2) The protection of phonograms does not
limit or cause prejudice to the protection of
copyrights.

articles.heading: Duration for protection of a broadcast (1) A broadcast is protected for a period of 25 years from the first month of the
articles.text:
year that follows the year in which the
broadcast took place.
(2) The protection of a broadcast does not
limit or cause prejudice to the
protection of copyrights.
359

articles.heading: Free ephemeral use of sounds and images performance by a broadcasting organisation (1) Authorisation to make fixations of
articles.text:
performances and broadcasts, to
reproduce such fixations on phonograms
published for commercial purposes is not
required when ephemeral fixations or
reproductions are made by broadcasting
organisation using its own means and for
its own broadcasts.
(2) However, the following acts require
authorisation:
(a) each broadcast of a fixation of a
performance or its reproductions;
(b) each broadcast of fixed broadcasts, or
of reproduction of such fixation.
(3) Audio visual broadcasts recorded or its
reproductions, the fixation and its
reproductions are destroyed within six
months following the period when
recording took place and reproductions
360
of works protected by copyrights, except
a single copy that is kept for the exclusive
purposes of conservation of archives and
constitution of documentation.

articles.heading: Rights of a performing artist (1) A performing artist has the exclusive right to carry out or to authorise the following
articles.text:
acts:
(a) to broadcast his or her performance,
except if the broadcasting:
(i) is made from a fixation of the
performance which the performer has
authorised to be made;
(ii) is a re-broadcasting authorised by the
broadcasting organisation initially
broadcasting the performance;
(b) distribution to the public of the
performance, except if such a
distribution is made from:
361
(i) a fixation based on the recorded sounds
or images of performance;
(ii) a broadcasting of the performance;
(c) fixation of unfixed performance;
(d) direct or indirect reproduction of a
fixation of his or her performance;
(e) fixation of his or her performance, or of
copies thereof, to the public by sale or
other transfer of ownership;
(f) rental to the public of a fixation of his
or her performance, or copies thereof;
(g) communication to the public of a fixed
performance in phonogram in such a
way that the public may access them
from a place or at a time individually
chosen by them.
362
(2) If the performer authorised fixation of a
performance in an audio-visual fixation,
the producer has the exclusive right to
authorise the use of the performance fixed
in the audio-visual work, unless otherwise
agreed.
(3) Subject to the rights of the producer, the
performer has the right to receive equitable
remuneration or royalties in respect of any
broadcasting, communication to the public,
rental or making available to the public of
his or her performance fixed in an audiovisual work.

articles.heading: Rights of phonogram producers (1) A phonogram producer has the exclusive right to carry out or to authorise the
articles.text:
following acts:
(a) direct or indirect reproduction of the
phonogram;
(b) distribution of copies of the phonogram
to the public by sale or other transfer of
363
rights on the work;
(c) rental of copies of the phonogram to the
public;
(d) communication of the phonogram to
the public, by wire or wireless, in such
a way that a person may access it from
a place or at a time chosen by that
person.
(2) The right of distribution under
Subparagraph (b) of paragraph (1) of this
Article does not apply to the original or a
copy of the work that has been put on the
market or has been subject to a sale or other
transfer of rights anywhere in the world
authorised by the owner of the copyright.

articles.heading: Rights of a broadcasting organisation A broadcasting organisation has the exclusive right to carry out or to authorise any of the
Limitations of broadcasting authorisation An authorisation to a broadcasting organisation to broadcast, unless otherwise
articles.text:
stipulated in the contract does not imply the
provision of the following:
(a) authorisation to other broadcasting
organisations to broadcast the
performance;
(b) authorisation to fix sounds and images
or performance ;
(c) authorisation to reproduce fixed sounds
and images or performance;
(d) authorisation to fix sounds and images
or a performance and to reproduce such
365
a fixation or the authorisation to
broadcast the performance from the
fixation or its reproductions.

articles.heading: Adequate remuneration for phonogram broadcasting or disclosure (1) The producer of a phonogram
articles.text:
published for commercial purposes and
broadcasted or disclosed to the public
through any other means is provided
with an adequate remuneration that is
shared between him or her and the
performing artist.
(2) The adequate remuneration referred to
in Paragraph (1) of this Article is
equitably shared unless provided
otherwise in the contract between the
producer of phonogram and the artist
performer.

articles.heading: Free use of related rights (1) The following acts are carried out without authorisation of performing artist,
articles.text:
phonogram producer or broadcasting
366
organisation and without remuneration:
(a) using short extracts of phonogram,
performance or broadcast for reporting
current events;
(b) reproduction of phonogram,
performance or broadcast solely for
scientific research;
(c) reproduction of phonogram,
performance or broadcast solely for the
purpose of face-to-face teaching
activities, except for performances and
sound recordings which have been
published as teaching or instructional
materials;
(d) using a phonogram, performance or a
broadcast for private purposes;
(e) reproduction of phonogram,
performance or broadcast by library
and documentation services free of
charge;
367
(f) using phonogram, performance or
broadcast for justice or administrative
purposes;
(g) reproduction and broadcast of
phonogram, performance or broadcast
for a person who is blind, visually
impaired or print disabled.
(2) The free use referred to in Paragraph (1) of
this Article does limit the ordinary use of
the work or right enjoyment by the
copyright owner.
CHAPTER III: COMMON PROVISIONS
TO COPYRIGHTS AND RELATED
RIGHTS

articles.heading: Collection and distribution of licence remunerations (1) The competent authority collects licence
articles.text:
remunerations and other proceeds from
exploitation of works, copyrights and
related rights and distributes the same
among rights owners.
368
(2) An Order of the Minister in charge of
Culture determines modalities for the
collection and distribution of
remunerations and other proceeds from
exploitation of works, copyrights and
related rights.

articles.heading: Prohibitions with regard to technical measures for protection of a work (1) For the purposes of protecting technical
articles.text:
measures for copyrights and related rights,
it is prohibited to:
(a) circumvent effective technical
measures for protection of a work;
(b) produce, import, distribute, sell, rent,
advertise for sale or rental, or possess
devices, products, components or
services for commercial purposes that
are promoted, advertised or marketed
for the purpose of circumventing
effective technical measures of
protection of a work.
(2) However, the right owner, upon request by
the person with the right to use a work
without being subjected to authorization in
369
circumstances provided for in Articles 288,
290, 291, 292, 294, 295, 296, 297, 298, 300
and 346 of this Law, waiver technical
measures for protection of a work to allow
its use in accordance with the law.

articles.heading: Effective technical measures for protection of a work Technical protection measures are effective if
articles.text:
the use of a work or object of related right
protected is controlled by the right owner
through application of an access control or
protection process, such as encryption,
scrambling or other transformation of the work
or other subject matter, or a copy control
mechanism, which, in the normal course of its
operation, achieves the protection objective.

articles.heading: Prohibitions related to copyright management information (1) The following acts related to copyrights
articles.text:
management information are prohibited:
370
(a) remove or alter any rights management
information without the consent of the
rights owner;
(b) distribute, import for distribution,
broadcast or communicate to the public
works or other subject- matter
protected from which rights
management information has been
removed or altered without the
authorisation of the rights owner.
(2) However, provisions of Paragraph (1)
of this Article do not apply to
governmental activities for public
order or security.
TITLE IV: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
RIGHTS ENFORCEMENT MEASURES,
OFFENCES AND SANCTIONS
CHAPTER ONE: INTELLECTUAL
PROPERTY RIGHTS ENFORCEMENT
MEASURES
371
Section One: Provisional measure in
relation to intellectual property

articles.heading: Request and ordering of a provisional measure in relation to intellectual property Upon a request by an industrial property title
articles.text:
holder, a copyright holder, a related rights
holder or a licensee, the competent court may
order a provisional measure to prevent an
unlawful act from occurring, or to preserve
relevant evidence in regard to an alleged
infringement.

articles.heading: Conditions for ordering a provisional measure (1) The competent court may order a provisional measure without hearing the
articles.text:
defendant where:
(a) any delay in ordering a measure on
an infringement of any intellectual
property right or in preserving
relevant evidence in regard to an
alleged infringement is likely to
372
cause irreparable harm to the right
holder;
(b) any reasonably available evidence
indicates that the applicant is the
right holder and that the applicant’s
right is being infringed or that such
infringement is imminent;
(c) the applicant provides a security or
equivalent assurance sufficient to
protect the defendant and to prevent
abuse.
(2) The court takes a decision within three
working days from the date of receipt of
the complaint. Where a provisional
measure has been adopted without hearing
the other party, the competent court gives
notice to both parties affected, without
delay.
(3) An Order of the Minister determines the
amount of guarantee or equivalent
assurance provided for in Paragraph (1),
Subparagraph (c) of this Article.
373

articles.heading: Review of a provisional measure (1) If a provisional measure has been ordered in accordance with Article 355,
articles.text:
the defendant may file a request for
review with the competent court within
15 days from the notification of the
measure.
(2) In reviewing the proceedings, the
competent court gives both parties an
opportunity of being heard and may
confirm, modify or revoke the decision
within two working days following the
day after the reception of the claim of
the request for review.

articles.heading: Revocation of a provisional measure Upon request by the defendant, the competent court may revoke a provisional measure if the
articles.text:
applicant does not initiate proceedings leading
to a decision on the merits of the case within
31 days from the notification of a provisional
measure.
374
Section 2: Corrective measures in relation
to intellectual property

articles.heading: Request and ordering of corrective measures in relation to industrial property Upon request by the industrial property owner
articles.text:
or a licensee, the competent court may order:
(a) cessation of release and advertisement
of counterfeit mark goods or goods
infringing the industrial property
owner’s rights into the channels of
commerce;
(b) that the goods bearing counterfeit
marks or otherwise infringing the
industrial property owner’s rights be
disposed of without compensation
outside the channels of commerce in
such a manner as to avoid any harm
caused to the right owner. A simple
removal of marks unlawfully affixed to
the goods is not sufficient, other than in
exceptional cases, to permit release of
the goods into the channels of
commerce;
375
(c) that materials or instruments that were
used or which may be used in the
creation or manufacture of goods with
imitative marks or goods otherwise
infringing the industrial property
owner’s rights be disposed of outside
the channels of commerce without
compensation in order to avoid the
risks of infringement of the owner’s
rights;
(d) seizure, forfeiture or destruction of the
infringing goods and of any materials
or instruments used in the manufacture
of the infringing goods.

articles.heading: Request and ordering of a corrective measure in relation to copyrights and related rights (1) Upon request by a copyright holder, a
articles.text:
related rights holder or a licensee, the
competent court may order:
(a) cessation of unlawful act or act
infringing the copyright;
376
(b) seizure, forfeiture or destruction of
copies of works or phonograms made
or imported or suspected of being
made or imported without the
authorisation of the intellectual
property right holder;
(c) seizure, forfeiture or destruction of the
packaging of copies of works or
phonograms, materials or instruments
used for the making of such copies of
works, and the documents, or business
papers referring to such copies;
(d) disposal outside the channels of
commerce of copies, phonograms and
their packaging that are used to
commit or continue to commit acts of
infringement of the intellectual
property right holder;
(e) disposal outside the channels of
commerce of the materials or
instruments that are likely to be used
to commit or continue to commit acts
of infringement of the intellectual
property right holder.
377
(2) The seizure, forfeiture or destruction in
accordance with Paragraph (1) of this
Article is not applicable to copies and
their packaging that were acquired by a
third party in good faith.

articles.heading: Damages (1) The competent court may order the infringer of rights of an intellectual property right holder to pay him or her
articles.text:
adequate damages where the infringer of
rights of an intellectual property right
holder knew or had reasonable grounds to
know that he or she was engaged in an
activity that infringes the rights of an
intellectual property right holder.
(2) The competent court may order the
infringer of rights of an intellectual
property right holder to pay him or her
the profits obtained by him or her by
engaging, knowingly or with reasonable
grounds to know, in an activity that
infringes his or her rights.
(3) Where the competent court finds that the
applicant filed the complaint in bad faith,
it orders him or her to pay the defendant
adequate compensation for the injury
suffered.
378

articles.heading: Right of information Upon request by the intellectual property right holder, the protected right holder or any other
articles.text:
interested person, the competent court may
order the infringer of rights of an intellectual
property right holder to inform the intellectual
property right holder of the identity of third
persons involved in the production and
distribution of the infringing goods or services
and of their channels of distribution.

articles.heading: Burden of proof in relation to the process patent (1) If the subject matter of a patent is a
articles.text:
process for obtaining a product, the
competent court can order the
defendant to prove that the process to
obtain an identical product is different
from the patented process.
379
(2) Any identical product when produced
without the consent of the patent owner
is, in the absence of proof to the
contrary, deemed to have been
obtained by the patented process for
one of the following reasons:
(a) if the product obtained by the
patented process is new;
(b) if there is a substantial likelihood
that the identical product was made
by the process and the owner of the
patent has been unable through
reasonable efforts to determine the
process actually used.
(3) In requiring the production of proof,
the competent court before which the
proceedings take place do not disclose
manufacturing and business secrets of
the alleged infringer.
Section 3: Special requirements related to
border measures
380
Subsection One: Measures that may be
taken by the customs authority

articles.heading: Request for suspension of the release of goods into free circulation (1) Upon a request in writing by a right holder
articles.text:
who has valid grounds for suspecting that
the importation of counterfeit goods or
upon own initiative, the customs authority
may suspend the customs clearance
procedures and release into free circulation
of goods.
(2) The customs authority may require the
applicant who requested the suspension of
the customs clearance procedures and
release into free circulation of goods to
provide adequate evidence to prove that
there was a counterfeit of goods and to
supply a sufficiently detailed description of
the goods to make them readily
recognisable by the customs authority.

articles.heading: Goods considered as counterfeit Goods are considered as counterfeit if
articles.text:
381
(a) they infringe a registered mark or a
geographical indication used in relation
to such goods if the use of such goods
for commercial purposes in the
Republic of Rwanda would infringe the
rights conferred by the mark or
geographical indication;
(b) they infringe a copyright or related
right if they are copies made without
the consent of the right holder or a
person duly authorised by the right
holder in the country of production and
which were made directly or indirectly
from an article where the making of
that copy in the Republic of Rwanda
would have constituted an
infringement of a copyright or a related
right;
(c) in relation to any other right protected,
their importation or circulation in the
channels of commerce would result in
acts constituting an infringement of
intellectual property right.

articles.heading: Notice of suspension of the release of goods into free circulation (1) The suspension of the release of goods
articles.text:
into free circulation by the customs
382
authority upon own initiative or upon
request by the right holder is notified to
the right holder and to the importer.
(2) The notice referred to in Paragraph (1)
of this Article is served within five
working days from the date on which
the decision of suspension was made.

articles.heading: Inspection and information on counterfeit goods (1) Without prejudice to the protection of confidential information, the customs
articles.text:
authority may allow the protected right
holder, the owner, the importer or the
consignee to inspect the goods of
which the release into circulation has
been suspended and to remove samples
for inspection, testing and analysis, in
order to substantiate each party’s
claims.
(2) If the release of goods into circulation
is suspended, the customs authority
informs the protected right holder of
the identity of the owner, the importer
or the consignee, as well as the goods
and their quantity.
383

articles.heading: Provision of a security for suspension of release of counterfeit goods into free circulation
articles.text:
(1) The customs authority suspends the
release of goods into free circulation after
the applicant provides a security or
equivalent assurance.
(2) The security referred to in Paragraph (1)
of this Article is intended to:
(a) cover expenditures related to the
suspension of release into free
circulation by the custom authority;
(b) pay the importer appropriate
compensation if it is found that there
was no infringement.
(3) If the release of goods into circulation has
been suspended by the customs authority
upon own initiative, the security is
provided by the owner within 10 working
days from the notification. If the security
is not provided, the goods are released.
384
(4) An Order of the Minister determines the
amount of security or equivalent
assurance provided for goods of which the
release into circulation is sought.

articles.heading: Duration of suspension of release of goods into free circulation (1) The applicant for suspension of release
articles.text:
of goods into free circulation informs
the customs authority that he or she has
initiated proceedings before the
competent court or that a provisional
measure prolonging the suspension of
the release has been taken by the
competent court within 10 working
days after the protected right holder has
been served notice of the suspension of
release of goods into circulation.
(2) If the conditions provided for in
Paragraph (1) of this Article have not
been complied with, the goods are
released provided that all other
formalities of customs clearance have
been complied with.
(3) If the application for suspension of the
release of goods involves industrial
designs, patents, layout-designs or
trade secrets into free circulation that
have been suspended by the customs
385
authority, and the period of suspension
of the goods provided for in Paragraph
(1) of this Article has expired without
the decision of the court to release the
goods, and provided that all other
conditions for importation have been
complied with, the owner, importer, or
consignee of such goods is entitled to
their release on the posting of a security
in an amount sufficient to protect the
right holder for any infringement.
(4) If the applicant for suspension of the
release of goods into circulation fails to
initiate a civil action before the
competent court within 14 days from
the date of suspension of the release of
goods into circulation, the security is
released.

articles.heading: Non liability of customs authority The customs authority and its employees are not liable for any action taken in compliance
articles.text:
with formalities of customs clearance of goods
and suspension of their release into free
386
circulation, even if it is later proved that goods
infringing a protected right holder have been
released into free circulation.

articles.heading: Goods not subject to special border measures Special border measures do not apply to the following
articles.text:
(a) small quantities of goods of a noncommercial nature;
(b) goods that are in transit on the territory of
the Republic of Rwanda.
Subsection 2: Measures ordered by courts

articles.heading: Grounds for court’s measure The competent court may order a measure aimed at preventing any infringement of a right
articles.text:
to goods on the following grounds:
(a) if such goods infringe intellectual
property rights protected in the
Republic of Rwanda;
387
(b) if the processing of such goods or their
circulation on the Rwandan market is
an act of unfair competition.

articles.heading: Measure ordered by a court (1) If the competent court determines that a right to goods has been infringed, it may
articles.text:
order:
(a) the disposal of such goods outside the
Rwandan market;
(b) the suspension of commercial activities
for goods that infringe intellectual
property rights;
(c) the destruction of such goods.
(2) Before an order for destruction of the goods
infringing rights and their disposal outside
the market is made, the court considers the
proportionality between the seriousness of
the infringement and the remedies ordered
as well as the interests of third parties.
388
CHAPTER II: OFFENCES AND
SANCTIONS

articles.heading: Infringement of intellectual property rights Any person who uses intellectual property without right owner’s consent and performs
articles.text:
any of the following acts intentionally and for
commercial purposes:
(a) infringing the copyrights or related rights
protected;
(b) producing, selling, offering for sale,
offering for rent, owning or importing on
the territory of Rwanda the alleged
infringing goods;
(c) uses a mark of another person; commits
an offence. Upon conviction, he or she is
liable to imprisonment for a term of not
less than 3 years but not more than 5
years and a fine of not less than FRW
3,000,000 but not more than FRW
5,000,000.
389

articles.heading: Performing or publishing a work in forgery manner Any person who performs or publishes a work
articles.text:
in a forgery manner commits an offence. Upon
conviction, he or she is liable to imprisonment
for a term of not less than 3 years but not more
than 5 years and a fine of not less than FRW
7,000,000 but not more than FRW 10,000,000.

articles.heading: Fraudulent use of the name of an author or his or her distinctive sign on a literary, artistic or scientific work
articles.text:
Any person who fraudulently uses the name of
an author or his or her distinctive sign on a
literary, artistic or scientific work, commits an
offence. Upon conviction, he or she is liable to
imprisonment for a term of not less than 3
years but not more than 5 years and a fine of
not less than FRW 7,000,000 but not more than
FRW 10,000,000.
390

articles.heading: Sale of counterfeit products Any person who knowingly sells counterfeit products, commits an offence. Upon
articles.text:
conviction, he or she is liable to a fine of not
less than FRW 300,000 but not more than
FRW 500,000.

articles.heading: Communication to the public of a protected work without authorisation Any person who broadcasts or communicates
articles.text:
to the public a protected work by any means of
communication channels, without prior
authorisation of right owner or his or her
representative, commits an offence. Upon
conviction, he or she is liable to a fine of not
less than FRW 1,000,000 but not more than
FRW 2,000,000.

articles.heading: Granting or giving another person the right to perform a work without authorisation of the owner
articles.text:
Any person who grants or gives another person
the right to perform a work without
authorisation of the right owner or his or her
representative, or any other person who acts
under false authorisation, commits an offence.
Upon conviction, he or she is liable to
391
imprisonment for a term of not less than 1 year
but not more than 2 years and a fine of not less
than FRW 500,000 but not more than FRW
1,000,000.

articles.heading: Steal or use by fraudulent manner a formula of invention Any person who steals or uses by fraudulent
articles.text:
manner a formula of invention, commits an
offence. Upon conviction, he or she is liable to
imprisonment for a term of not less than 3
years but not more than 5 years and a fine of
not less than FRW 7,000,000 but not more than
FRW 10,000,000.

articles.heading: Act of unfair competition with respect to intellectual property Any person who performs an act of unfair
articles.text:
competition with respect to intellectual
property, commits an offence. Upon
conviction, he or she is liable to a fine of not
less than FRW 7,000,000 but not more than
FRW 10,000,000.
392

articles.heading: Punishment of a corporate body or a legal entity A corporate body or a legal entity that commits
articles.text:
one of the offences referred to in Articles 373,
374, 375, 376, 378, 379 and 380 of this Law
commits an offence. Upon conviction, it is
liable to a fine whose amount is ten times that
which is provided in the respective Article.

articles.heading: Additional sanctions In addition to sanctions provided for under this Law, the court may also order the seizure,
articles.text:
destruction or confiscation of items used in the
commission of any of the offences provided for
under this Law.

are deposited.
